1. Install SEH (Structured Exception Handling) frame for cleanup on exception
2. Zero initialize base unit fields (offsets +0x0 and +0x4)
3. Construct first element array at offset +0x4c (76 bytes):
   - Array contains 4 ListNode elements, 12 bytes each
   - Calls InitializeListNode constructor for each element
4. Update initialization phase to 2 (for exception recovery tracking)
5. Construct second element array at offset +0x58 (88 bytes):
   - Same structure: 4 ListNode elements, 12 bytes each
6. Update initialization phase to 3
7. Construct third element array at offset +0x64 (100 bytes):
   - Same structure: 4 ListNode elements, 12 bytes each
8. Update initialization phase to 4
9. Initialize circular linked list node at offset +0x1c0 (448 bytes):
   - Create empty self-referencing linked list (next points to self)
   - Set magic integrity sentinel to ~(address) for validation
10. Clean up SEH frame and restore previous exception handler
11. Return pointer to initialized unit

Parameters:
pUnit: Pointer to uninitialized UnitAny structure (96 bytes)
       Must have sufficient allocated memory for all arrays and linked list

Returns:
UnitAny *: Pointer to the newly initialized unit (same as input pUnit)

Special Cases:
- SEH Exception Handling: If exception occurs during construction, phase tracker
  (offset +0x10 in stack) determines which destructors to run for cleanup
- Magic Offset 0x1c0: Linked list node for unit management/tracking
- Phase Values: 1-4 mark completion of each construction stage; 0xffffffff signals
  successful completion or exception state
- Constructor/Destructor: ListNode elements use custom constructors (InitializeListNode)
  and destructors (ProcessExceptionFrameUnlinking) for resource management

Offset | Size | Field Name | Type | Description
0x0 | 4 | field_0x0 | dword | First initialization field
0x4 | 4 | field_0x4 | dword | Second initialization field
0x4c | 48 | arrayFirst | ListNode[4] | First array of list nodes (12 bytes each)
0x58 | 48 | arraySecond | ListNode[4] | Second array of list nodes (12 bytes each)
0x64 | 48 | arrayThird | ListNode[4] | Third array of list nodes (12 bytes each)
0x1c0 | 12 | listNode | ListNode | Circular linked list node for tracking

0x6FBF52D0.name: DestructorDestroyStructureWithArrays
0x6FBF52D0.comment:
Destructor for composite structure with nested objects and arrays

Algorithm:
1. Save current exception handler from FS:[0x0] (thread-local exception chain)
2. Set up new exception frame with base address at ESP and handler code at 0x6fc31ab0
3. Initialize exception cleanup state flag to 3 (for exception unwinding tracking)
4. Call object destructor on embedded object at offset +0x1c0 (12 bytes)
5. Set exception state to 2 and call vector destructor on first array
   - Array at offset +0x190: 4 elements with stride 0xc bytes each (48 bytes total)
6. Set exception state to 1 and call vector destructor on second array
   - Array at offset +0x160: 4 elements with stride 0xc bytes each (48 bytes total)
7. Set exception state to 0 and call vector destructor on third array
   - Array at offset +0x130: 4 elements with stride 0xc bytes each (48 bytes total)
8. Set exception state to 0xffffffff (sentinel indicating full cleanup)
9. Unlink exception frame node from chain to restore prior exception state
10. Restore prior exception handler pointer to FS:[0x0]
11. Pop saved ESI register and clean 0xc bytes from stack
12. Return to caller (callee cleanup via RET 0x4)

Parameters:
- pStructure: void pointer to composite structure containing:
  * Embedded object at offset +0x1c0 requiring destruction
  * Array 1 at offset +0x190 (4 objects, 0xc bytes each)
  * Array 2 at offset +0x160 (4 objects, 0xc bytes each)
  * Array 3 at offset +0x130 (4 objects, 0xc bytes each)

Returns:
- void: Function completes destruction sequence and returns to caller

Special Cases:
- Exception handling: State flags (3,2,1,0xffffffff) track which objects have been destroyed
  for proper unwinding if destructor throws during execution
- If exception occurs during any destructor call, the exception frame allows
  controlled unwinding of already-destroyed objects
- Vector destructor uses iterator pattern with stride and count parameters
- All destructors called with __stdcall convention
- FS:[0x0] is Windows x86 TEB (Thread Environment Block) exception chain pointer

0x6FBF5370.name: InitializeListNode
0x6FBF5370.comment:
Initializes a doubly-linked list node structure for circular linked list management.

Algorithm:
1. Set up SEH (Structured Exception Handling) exception frame (PUSH -0x1, PUSH handler)
2. Initialize pNode->reserved field to 0 (offset +0x0)
3. Calculate pNext pointer at offset +0x4 from base node address
4. Zero out pNext and pNode[2] fields (offset +0x4 and +0x8)
5. Set pNext to point to itself (circular list: node->pNext = &node->pNext)
6. Invert pNext address using bitwise NOT to create integrity sentinel
7. Store sentinel in pNode[2] (offset +0x8) for linked list validation
8. Restore SEH exception handler and return

Parameters:
- pNode: Pointer to uninitialized 12-byte ListNode structure to construct

Returns:
- void: No return value; structure is initialized in-place

Special Cases:
- SEH exception handling: Saves and restores FS:[0] for C++ exception support
- Circular linking: pNode->pNext points to the pNext field itself (empty list state)
- Sentinel value: Stored as ~(uint)pNextPtr for integrity checking during traversal
- Structure size: 12 bytes (0xc) with 3 dword fields
- Calling convention: __fastcall passes pNode in ECX register

Structure Layout:
Offset  Size  Field Name  Type        Description
------  ----  ----------  ----------  -----------
0x0     4     reserved    uint        Reserved/control field (initialized to 0)
0x4     4     pNext       pointer     Next node pointer (self-pointing for empty list)
0x8     4     sentinel    uint        Bitwise NOT of pNext for integrity validation
------
Total: 12 bytes (0xc)

0x6FBF53C0.name: ProcessExceptionFrameUnlinking
0x6FBF53C0.comment:
Unlinks exception frame from the SEH chain and processes cleanup operations.

Algorithm:
1. Save current FS:[0x0] exception handler pointer to stack
2. Install new exception handler frame at LAB_6fc31a3b
3. Set cleanupState to 3 (cleanup in progress marker)
4. Call ProcessExceptionListNodes() to handle pending linked list operations
5. Set cleanupState to 0xffffffff (cleanup complete marker)
6. Load pointer to next node from pFrameNode+4
7. If next node pointer is zero, skip to cleanup (check_node_pointer)
8. Load offset value from pFrameNode+8
9. Test offset sign (offset_sign_check):
   - If negative: calculate target as ~offset (direct inversion)
   - If non-negative: calculate target as (pFrameNode+4) + offset - node[4]
10. Store next node pointer at calculated target address (store_node_pointer)
11. Load next node's next pointer from target[0]
12. Load offset value from target[4]
13. Update target[4] with node offset value
14. Clear pFrameNode+4 to unlink from exception chain
15. Clear pFrameNode+8 to mark processing complete
16. Restore prior exception handler from FS:[0x0]
17. Return to caller (fastcall convention)

Parameters:
- pFrameNode (ECX): Pointer to exception frame structure
  +4: Pointer to next node in exception handler chain
  +8: Offset value for target address calculation

Returns:
- void: No return value, completes frame unlinking

Special Cases:
- Negative offset values use bitwise NOT (~) to derive direct address
- Positive offsets require subtraction of node offset before addition
- Exception state markers (3, 0xffffffff) track cleanup phases
- FS:[0x0] manages the Windows SEH (Structured Exception Handling) chain
- ProcessExceptionListNodes() handles cross-reference updates during unlinking
- Uses fastcall convention: parameter passed in ECX register, callee cleanup

0x6FBF5440.name: ReallocateArrayPool
0x6FBF5440.comment:
Reallocates player name array pool with new capacity and copies existing data.

Algorithm:
1. Load old buffer pointer from pArrayPool->buffer (offset +0x8)
2. Store new aligned capacity in pArrayPool->currentCount (offset +0x0)
3. Call Ordinal_405 (realloc) to resize old buffer to new capacity*128 bytes with -2 flags
4. Store reallocated buffer in pArrayPool->buffer (offset +0x8)
5. If realloc succeeded (pNewBuffer != 0), exit to success_exit
6. If realloc failed (pNewBuffer == 0), call Ordinal_401 (malloc) for new buffer with capacity*128 bytes
7. Store newly allocated buffer in pArrayPool->buffer (offset +0x8)
8. If old buffer is null (pOldBuffer == 0), skip to free_old_buffer (no data to copy)
9. Compare new capacity against old capacity from pArrayPool->maxCount (offset +0x4)
10. If new capacity > old capacity, use old capacity as copy limit
11. If copy limit is 0, skip copy_loop and go to free_old_buffer
12. Loop through each element from 0 to (copy_limit-1):
    a. Load source address: pArrayPool->buffer[index] (offset +0x8)
    b. Load destination address: pNewBuffer[index] (offset +0x8)
    c. If destination is null (no allocation for this element), skip to copy_loop_advance
    d. Copy 32 dwords (128 bytes) from source to destination using REP MOVSD
13. After copying all elements, call Ordinal_403 (free) to deallocate old buffer
14. Return void

Parameters:
pArrayPool - Pointer to ArrayPool structure (passed in EBX as implicit register parameter)
alignedCapacity - New capacity in array elements (passed in EAX)

Returns:
void - Function modifies array pool in place

ArrayPool Structure Layout:
Offset  Size  Field          Type     Description
+0x0    4     currentCount   dword    Current element count
+0x4    4     maxCount       dword    Maximum capacity before reallocation
+0x8    4     buffer         dword*   Pointer to element array (not the array itself)
+0xc    4     reserved       dword    Unused/reserved field

Element Format:
Each array element is 128 bytes (0x80). Player name data is stored in fixed 128-byte slots.

Special Cases:
- If old buffer is null (pOldBuffer == 0), skips copy phase and goes directly to cleanup
- If new capacity exceeds old capacity, only copies up to old capacity elements
- Uses copy limit logic to avoid accessing beyond old allocation bounds
- Magic: 128-byte element size (0x80) and 32-dword copy (0x20 dwords = 128 bytes)
- Allocation flags: -2 indicates special allocation context for player name pool
- Uses three allocation functions: Ordinal_405 (realloc), Ordinal_401 (malloc), Ordinal_403 (free)

0x6FBF595D.name: TypeInfoDestructor
0x6FBF595D.comment:
C++ type_info Virtual Destructor - RTTI type information cleanup

Algorithm:
1. Initialize SEH exception handling frame with size 0x8
2. Set up exception handling via __SEH_prolog call
3. Store this pointer in ESI for safe reference
4. Set vftable pointer at offset 0 to type_info class vtable
5. Acquire exclusive lock on global typeinfo state (lock level 0xe)
6. Load name/description string pointer from this+4 offset
7. Test if pointer is NULL to prevent invalid deallocation
8. If non-NULL, push pointer and call _free() to deallocate
9. Set exception frame cleanup state via OR with 0xffffffff
10. Release global typeinfo lock via ReleaseLockForTypeinfo()
11. Clean up exception handling frame via __SEH_epilog
12. Execute RET instruction to return to caller

Parameters:
  pThis (type_info *): Pointer to type_info object instance being destroyed

Returns:
  void: Destructor performs in-place cleanup with no return value

Special Cases:
  - NULL pointer at this+4 is handled safely, skip deallocation if NULL
  - Exception frame management prevents stack unwinding issues
  - Global lock ensures thread-safe typeinfo system state
  - __thiscall convention passes this pointer in ECX register

0x6FBF599A.name: ReleaseLockForTypeinfo
0x6FBF599A.comment:
Releases the critical section lock protecting type_info object state.

This function is a thin wrapper around LeaveCriticalSectionByIndex that
releases a specific critical section lock used by the type_info system.

Algorithm:
1. Push immediate lock index 0xe (14) onto the stack as function argument
2. Call LeaveCriticalSectionByIndex(0xe) to release the critical section
3. Clean up stack with POP ECX (stdcall calling convention requirement)
4. Execute RET instruction to return control to caller

Parameters:
None - The lock index (0xe) is passed as an immediate constant value,
not as a parameter from the caller. This is a fixed lock index that
always protects type_info object access synchronization.

Returns:
void - Function returns no value, it only performs the lock release.

Special Cases:
Lock index 0xe is reserved for type_info object synchronization and must
be released when type_info objects are destroyed. Failure to properly
release this lock could cause deadlocks or resource leaks.

0x6FBF59A3.name: TypeInfoScalarDeletingDestructor
0x6FBF59A3.signature: void * TypeInfoScalarDeletingDestructor(type_info * this, void * pThis, uint deleteFlag)
0x6FBF59A3.comment:
Scalar deleting destructor for type_info objects with optional memory deallocation.

This is a standard C++ scalar deleting destructor that combines type-specific destruction 
with optional object deallocation. The scalar variant processes a single object instance 
(as opposed to array destructor which handles multiple elements).

Algorithm:
1. Save ESI register to preserve it across function calls
2. Move implicit this pointer from ECX to ESI for safe preservation
3. Call TypeInfoDestructor to perform type-specific cleanup and destruction
4. Test bit 0 of deleteFlag parameter to determine memory deallocation behavior
5. If bit 0 set (deleteFlag & 1 != 0), call DeleteObject to deallocate the object's memory
6. Return the this pointer to the caller
7. Restore ESI register and return with 4-byte parameter cleanup

Parameters:
- pThis (ECX implicit): Pointer to type_info object to destruct
- deleteFlag (ESP+0x8): Flag controlling object deallocation. Bit 0 determines whether 
  to call delete after destruction. Common values: 0 = destructor only, 1 = destructor + delete

Returns:
- void *: The this pointer (original object address) in EAX

Special Cases:
- The function always calls TypeInfoDestructor regardless of deleteFlag value
- Memory deallocation only occurs if (deleteFlag & 1) != 0
- The returned pointer points to memory that may be deallocated if deleteFlag bit 0 was set
- This is a __thiscall function: implicit this in ECX, 4-byte stack parameter, RET 0x4 cleanup

Calling Convention:
__thiscall: First parameter (this) passed in ECX register, remaining parameters on stack, 
callee cleans up parameters with RET 0x4

0x6FBF5CC0.name: SelectionSortPartition
0x6FBF5CC0.signature: void SelectionSortPartition(byte * pArray, int elementSize, void * pCompareFunc)
0x6FBF5CC0.comment:
Selection sort partitioning helper used by qsort implementation.

Algorithm:
1. Check if array has at least 2 elements (start < end), exit if not
2. Initialize ESI to point to first element + element_size (next position)
3. For each partition round (outer loop):
   a. Initialize pMinElement to current array start position
   b. Scan remaining elements (inner loop) calling comparison function
   c. If comparison returns positive, update pMinElement pointer
   d. After inner loop completes, check if minimum element differs from start
   e. If different, swap minimum element with current position byte-by-byte
   f. Move partition boundary down by element_size
   g. Repeat until all elements partitioned
4. Return to caller when partition complete

Parameters:
- pArray (EAX): Pointer to array end (upper bound of partition range)
- elementSize (EBP): Size of each array element in bytes
- pCompareFunc ([ESP+0x24]): Function pointer to comparison function
  Signature: int compare(byte *pElement1, byte *pElement2)
  Returns: positive if pElement1 > pElement2, 0 or negative otherwise

Returns:
- void (no return value)

Special Cases:
- If elementSize is 0, no swap occurs even if minimum differs
- Array traversal uses pointer arithmetic, not index calculation
- Comparison function receives pointers to actual elements, not indices
- Swap operation is byte-by-byte to handle arbitrary element sizes
- Selection sort has O(n²) time complexity for n elements

0x6FBF605E.name: DestructVectorElementsIterator
0x6FBF605E.signature: void DestructVectorElementsIterator(void * pVector, uint dwElementSize, int nElementCount, void * pDestructor)
0x6FBF605E.comment:
Destructively iterates through a vector/array backward, calling a destructor function on each element.
This is a C++ runtime helper used for exception-safe cleanup of dynamically allocated arrays.
The function uses Structured Exception Handling (SEH) to ensure proper cleanup if an exception occurs.

Algorithm:
1. Initialize SEH frame with __SEH_prolog (saves exception handler state)
2. Calculate ending address: pVector + (nElementCount * dwElementSize)
3. Initialize exception flags to zero (no exception occurred)
4. Loop backward through array elements:
   a. Decrement element counter
   b. If counter < 0, break from loop (all elements processed)
   c. Subtract element size from current address to move to previous element
   d. Call destructor function on current element via function pointer pDestructor
   e. Repeat from step 4a
5. After loop completes, mark successful completion (flag = 1)
6. Set exception flag to -1 (0xFFFFFFFF) indicating final state
7. Call ConditionalArrayUnwind for exception-safe cleanup
8. Execute __SEH_epilog to restore exception handler and return

Parameters:
pVector (EBP+0x8): Base pointer to the vector/array to be destructed
dwElementSize (EBP+0xC): Size in bytes of each element (stride)
nElementCount (EBP+0x10): Number of elements to destruct (iteration count)
pDestructor (EBP+0x14): Function pointer to destructor function (__thiscall convention)

Returns:
void - No return value; cleanup performed via side effects

Special Cases:
- nElementCount can be 0 (no elements to destruct, loop skipped)
- SEH frame allows exception handling during destructor calls
- ConditionalArrayUnwind handles partial destruction if exception occurs
- Uses IMUL to calculate offset: EAX = dwElementSize * nElementCount
- Element size typically 4 bytes (pointer) or size of the class/struct
- Negative element count or invalid size values will cause undefined behavior

Called By:
UnwindExceptionHandler, UnwindExceptionDestructor, DestructVectorWithExceptionHandler,
and other exception handling/cleanup routines

0x6FBF60A6.name: ConditionalArrayUnwind
0x6FBF60A6.signature: void ConditionalArrayUnwind(void * pArray, uint elementCount, int elementSize, _func_void_void_ptr * pDestructor)
0x6FBF60A6.comment:
Conditionally unwinds (destructs) an array of objects.

ALGORITHM:
1. Check if the unwind condition flag (stack local at [EBP - 0x1C]) is zero
2. If zero, call __ArrayUnwind with array parameters
3. Otherwise, skip the unwind and return immediately

PARAMETERS:
pArray (void *): Pointer to the base of the array to unwind
elementCount (uint): Number of elements in the array
elementSize (int): Size in bytes of each array element
pDestructor (_func_void_void_ptr *): Pointer to the element destructor function

RETURNS:
void: No return value

SPECIAL CASES:
- If the unwind condition flag is non-zero, the array is not unwound
- The unwind condition is stored in a local stack variable at [EBP - 0x1C]
- This is a C++ runtime helper used during exception handling for array destruction

CONTEXT:
Called from eh_vector_destructor_iterator as a wrapper that conditionally invokes
the array unwinding logic. This pattern is typical of C++ exception handling where
destructors may need to be conditionally applied based on construction state.

0x6FBF6108.name: ConditionalArrayUnwind
0x6FBF6108.comment:
Conditionally unwinds an array of objects if a counter reaches zero.

Algorithm:
1. Load counter value from [EBP - 0x20] and compare to zero
2. If counter is not zero, skip unwind and return (fast path)
3. If counter is zero, push 4 parameters onto stack:
   - [EBP + 0x8]: Object array pointer
   - [EBP + 0xC]: Element count
   - [EBP - 0x1C]: Element size or destructor reference
   - [EBP + 0x18]: Destructor function pointer
4. Call __ArrayUnwind to clean up array elements
5. Return to caller with stack cleaned

Parameters:
- IMPLICIT EBP: Frame pointer for access to caller's local variables

Returns:
- void: No return value

Special Cases:
- Fast path: If counter is non-zero, skips unwind immediately
- Unwind trigger: Only executes if counter reaches exactly zero
- Destructor callback: Fourth parameter is destructor function pointer

Structure Layout:
- [EBP + 0x8]: Array pointer
- [EBP + 0xC]: Element count
- [EBP + 0x18]: Destructor function pointer
- [EBP - 0x1C]: Element size or secondary destructor
- [EBP - 0x20]: Counter (zero triggers unwind)

0x6FBF6868.name: GetWideStringLength
0x6FBF6868.comment:
Calculate the length of a null-terminated wide character string.

Algorithm:
1. Load the input wide string pointer from the stack
2. Loop through each wide character (2 bytes per character):
   - Load the current wide character value (short)
   - Increment the pointer by 2 bytes (size of short)
   - Test if the loaded character is zero (null terminator)
   - Jump back to load the next character if not zero
3. When null terminator is found, calculate pointer distance from start to end
4. Divide the byte distance by 2 to convert to character count
5. Subtract 1 to exclude the null terminator from the count
6. Return the character count in EAX

Parameters:
  pWideString: Pointer to null-terminated wide character string (short array)

Returns:
  int: Number of wide characters excluding the null terminator
       Returns -1 if the string contains only a null terminator (empty string)

Special Cases:
  - Empty string (immediate null terminator at pWideString): Returns -1
  - Single character string: Returns 0 (after subtracting null terminator)
  - String calculation uses pointer arithmetic for efficiency

0x6FBF687E.name: ConvertWideStringToMultibyte
0x6FBF687E.signature: int ConvertWideStringToMultibyte(pthreadlocinfo pLocaleInfo, LPSTR pDestBuffer, LPCWSTR pSourceString, uint dwDestSize)
0x6FBF687E.comment:
Converts a wide character (Unicode) string to a multibyte string using a specified code page and locale.

Algorithm:
1. Initialize stack canary guard value via XOR with frame pointer for overflow detection
2. Validate destination buffer pointer and size parameters
3. If destination buffer is NULL:
   - Call WideCharToMultiByte with NULL buffer to calculate required output size
   - Return size or error code based on conversion result
4. If destination buffer is provided:
   - Branch on locale mode flag (pLocaleInfo->lc_category[0].wlocale):
     a. ASCII-only mode: Loop copying single bytes, reject chars > 0xFF
     b. Variable-width mode: Scan for null terminator, calculate length, convert with bounded size
     c. Standard mode: Call WideCharToMultiByte with -1 (null-terminated)
5. Handle insufficient buffer error (0x7a):
   - Fall back to character-by-character conversion using 8-byte temp buffer
   - Verify each converted chunk fits in output buffer
   - Copy bytes to destination, stop on null terminator
6. Validate conversion results:
   - Check used_default flag (indicates lossy conversion or unmappable char)
   - Verify null terminator not replaced by default character
7. On any error: Call GetThreadErrorNumberPointer to set error code 0x2a
8. Verify stack canary before return to detect overflow

Parameters:
  pLocaleInfo: Pointer to locale info structure with code page (offset 0x4) and mode flag (offset 0x14)
  pDestBuffer: Destination multibyte buffer (or NULL to get required size)
  pSourceString: Source wide character string (null-terminated)
  nDestSize: Maximum size of destination buffer in bytes

Returns:
  Positive: Byte count of converted string (including null terminator)
  Zero: Buffer too small or conversion failure
  Negative: Error condition, error code set via GetThreadErrorNumberPointer

Special Cases:
  ERROR_INSUFFICIENT_BUFFER (0x7a): Triggers fallback char-by-char conversion
  Wide char > 0xFF in ASCII mode: Immediate error
  NULL destination: Returns required size without conversion
  Null terminator handling: Verified in output to ensure proper string termination
  Default character substitution: Detected and reported as error condition
  Stack overflow protection: XOR canary verified before return

Structure Layout:
  Offset  Size  Field Name              Type         Description
  0x0     4     lc_codepage             DWORD        Code page for WideCharToMultiByte
  0x4     4     lc_reserved1            pointer      Reserved field
  0x8     4     lc_reserved2            pointer      Reserved field
  0xC     4     lc_reserved3            pointer      Reserved field
  0x10    4     lc_reserved4            pointer      Reserved field
  0x14    4     lc_category.wlocale     pointer      Mode flag: NULL=ASCII, non-NULL=multibyte

0x6FBF6A28.name: ConvertWideStringToMultibyteChar
0x6FBF6A28.signature: void ConvertWideStringToMultibyteChar(LPSTR pDestBuffer, LPCWSTR pWideString, uint dwMaxLen)
0x6FBF6A28.comment:
Wrapper for wide-to-multibyte string conversion with locale checking

Algorithm:
1. Call __getptd() to retrieve current thread's local storage pointer
2. Load cached locale info from thread data structure at offset +0x64
3. Compare cached locale with global thread locale pointer g_pThreadLocInfoPtr
4. If locales differ, call ___updatetlocinfo() to update locale data
5. Push all three string conversion parameters onto stack in reverse order
6. Push locale info pointer as first implicit parameter
7. Call ConvertWideStringToMultibyte to perform actual conversion
8. Adjust stack by 0x10 bytes to clean up parameters
9. Return control to caller

Parameters:
pDestBuffer (LPSTR) - Destination buffer for converted multibyte character string
pWideString (LPCWSTR) - Source Unicode wide character string to convert
dwMaxLen (uint) - Maximum size of destination buffer in bytes (typically 0xff/255)

Returns:
void - No direct return value; conversion result stored in pDestBuffer

Special Cases:
- NULL pWideString is handled gracefully by ConvertWideStringToMultibyte
- Locale changes automatically detected and updated on each call
- Buffer overflow occurs silently if dwMaxLen < converted string length
- Empty wide string (L"") produces empty multibyte string in buffer

0x6FBF6D6D.name: ValidateGameConfig
0x6FBF6D6D.comment:
Validates game configuration by comparing expected config strings.

Algorithm:
1. Check if validation buffer (g_pConfigValidationBuffer) is already allocated
2. If not allocated, allocate 0x351 bytes using malloc; return NULL if allocation fails
3. Initialize buffer as empty string by setting first byte to null terminator
4. Append initial config entry 0 to the buffer using StringConcatenate
5. For entries 1 through 4:
   - Call StringConcatenate to append entry to buffer
   - Compare appended string against expected value from g_ConfigExpectedStrings using strcmp
   - If comparison fails (strings differ), set allEntriesMatch flag to false
6. After processing all 5 entries, check validation result:
   - If all entries matched expected values: free buffer, zero g_pConfigValidationBuffer, return default config pointer
   - If any entry mismatched: return pointer to validation buffer containing actual config
7. Return NULL if memory allocation fails

Parameters:
None - operates on global configuration state

Returns:
uint* - Pointer to validation buffer if config differs from expected
        Pointer to default config (g_DefaultConfigPointer) if validation passes
        NULL if memory allocation fails

Special Cases:
- Buffer persistence: Allocation is checked at function start; same buffer reused across multiple calls
- Memory cleanup: Buffer freed only when config matches expected values, otherwise retained for caller inspection
- Entry count: Fixed at 5 entries (indices 0-4); loop bounds strictly enforced

0x6FBF6E47.name: NormalizeLocaleString
0x6FBF6E47.signature: char * NormalizeLocaleString(char * szLocaleString, char * szLocaleCodeOutput, void * pLocaleInfo1, void * pLocaleInfo2)
0x6FBF6E47.comment:
Normalizes and converts locale/encoding names to internal representations.

Algorithm:
1. Validate input locale string is not null; return null if null
2. Check if locale string is exactly "C" (single character with null terminator)
3. If "C" locale: set output code byte to 0x43, zero all info output parameters
4. For non-"C" locales: validate string length does not exceed 0x81 bytes
5. Check if locale matches first known preset string (g_szLocaleCodeBuffer)
6. Check if locale matches second known preset string (g_szNormalizedLocaleString)
7. If not a known preset, convert locale string to internal format using ___lc_strtolc
8. Call ___get_qualified_locale to validate and qualify the converted locale
9. Store word from g_wLocaleInfoWord into g_dwLocaleInfoStorage
10. Convert locale info array back to string using ___lc_lctostr
11. Validate converted string is not empty and does not exceed 0x81 bytes
12. If validation fails, use fallback locale (g_szDefaultLocaleFallback)
13. Clear normalization flag (g_bLocaleNormalizationFlag = 0)
14. Copy normalized string to g_szNormalizedLocaleString using strncpy
15. Copy locale info1 (6 bytes) to output parameter if provided
16. Copy locale info2 (4 bytes) to output parameter if provided
17. Call CopyString to generate normalized locale code and store in output
18. Verify stack canary before returning to detect buffer overflow
19. Return pointer to locale code buffer or null on failure

Parameters:
  pLocaleString (const char*): Input locale name string (e.g., "en_US", "C", "de_DE")
  pLocaleCodeOutput (char*): Output buffer for normalized locale code (4+ bytes)
  pLocaleInfo1 (void*): Output pointer for LC_STRINGS info structure (6 bytes)
  pLocaleInfo2 (void*): Output pointer for additional locale info (4 bytes)

Returns:
  Pointer to normalized locale code buffer on success
  NULL pointer on failure (invalid input, conversion error, or string validation failure)

Special Cases:
  - Locale "C" receives special-case handling with code 0x43
  - Maximum input string length is 0x81 (129) bytes
  - Fallback locale used if converted string validation fails
  - Stack canary verification protects against buffer overflow
  - Uses global state: g_szLocaleCodeBuffer, g_szNormalizedLocaleString, g_wLocaleInfoWord, g_dwLocaleInfoStorage

Structure References:
  LC_STRINGS: 458-byte structure containing locale information (referenced in ___get_qualified_locale)

0x6FBF6FA7.name: ApplyLocaleConfiguration
0x6FBF6FA7.comment:
Applies a locale/language configuration setting to the game, with full validation and rollback support.

Algorithm:
1. Normalize input locale string to standard format via NormalizeLocaleString()
2. Return early if normalization fails
3. Compare normalized string against current locale stored at g_pLocaleConfigData[ESI*3]
4. Skip update if strings are identical
5. Allocate memory for new locale string (length + 1 bytes)
6. Call internal function to process string into new locale data
7. Update locale configuration at g_pLocaleConfigData[ESI*3] and value at g_dwLocaleValueArray[ESI]
8. Copy 6 bytes of locale metadata (codepage/flags) to/from g_LocaleMetadataArray[ESI*6]
9. If critical locale (ESI==2): perform character type validation
   - Search linked list at g_LocaleListHead for matching codepage entry
   - If found at index 5, classify ASCII characters 0x00-0x7F via ___crtGetStringTypeA()
   - Mask to alphabetic bits only (0x01) and compare against g_dwCharTypeValidationTable
   - Store validation result (1=success, 0=failure) in g_LocaleListValidationStatus
10. If secondary locale (ESI==1): update g_dwSecondaryCodePage with new codepage
11. Call validation callback through g_pfnLocaleValidationCallback[ESI*0xc]
12. If callback succeeds (returns 0): free old locale data (unless it's default at 0x6fc400d0)
13. If callback fails (returns non-zero): rollback all changes and free new locale data

Parameters:
localeString (char *): Locale identifier string (e.g., "en_US", "fr_FR", "de_DE")

Returns:
int: Validation callback result (0 = success, non-zero = validation failed)

Special Cases:
- Skips processing if new locale matches current locale (optimization)
- Never frees default locale at 0x6fc400d0 to prevent dangling pointers
- Memory allocation failure silently returns without changes
- Critical locale type (ESI==2) requires additional character type validation
- Uses stack canary verification (g_dwStackGuardSeed) for buffer overflow detection

0x6FBF723B.name: ParseAndApplyLocaleConfig
0x6FBF723B.comment:
Parses and applies locale configuration strings in LC_* delimited or generic format.

Algorithm:
1. Check if mode parameter is non-zero (direct application mode)
2. If mode != 0, call ApplyLocaleConfiguration directly with localeString and exit
3. If localeString is NULL, return without applying any settings
4. Check if string starts with "LC_" prefix (3-byte sequence: 'L', 'C', '_')
5. If LC_* delimited format detected:
   a. Find semicolon delimiter using strpbrk to separate category from value
   b. Validate delimiter exists and is not at string start
   c. Search g_pszLocaleCategoryNames table for matching category name
   d. Extract category value from string between category name and next semicolon
   e. Copy extracted value to localeValueBuffer and null-terminate
   f. Call ApplyLocaleConfiguration with extracted value
   g. Increment appliedSettingsCount if application succeeded
   h. Continue to next category until string terminator or empty value found
6. If generic format (no LC_* prefix):
   a. Call NormalizeLocaleString to standardize format
   b. Iterate through g_pLocaleConfigData table entries (stride 0xC bytes per entry)
   c. Compare normalized string against each entry using strcmp
   d. Call ApplyLocaleConfiguration if entry matches or succeeds
   e. Set bValidationSucceeded to false if ApplyLocaleConfiguration fails
   f. Clear g_pLocaleConfigData if all entries validated successfully
7. If any settings were applied (appliedSettingsCount > 0), call ValidateGameConfig
8. Verify stack canary (XOR'd with buffer address) before return
9. Return appliedSettingsCount via EAX (non-zero = success)

Parameters:
  mode (ECX): 0=parse and apply localeString parameter, non-zero=apply localeString directly
  localeString (EDX): Pointer to locale configuration string

Returns:
  EAX: Non-zero if any locale settings applied successfully, 0 if no settings applied or NULL input

Special Cases:
  - NULL localeString pointer returns 0 without error
  - Empty localeString returns 0 without error
  - LC_* format parsing stops at first malformed entry (missing delimiter, unknown category)
  - Maximum 5 categories supported in LC_* format (categoryTableIndex limit)
  - Each category value limited to 15 characters (localeValueBuffer size - 1)
  - Semicolon (;) character terminates category values in LC_* format
  - Generic format requires successful NormalizeLocaleString to proceed
  - Stack canary check ensures no buffer overflow occurred during parsing

0x6FBF7418.name: InitializeLocaleWithCodePageAndConfig
0x6FBF7418.comment:
Initializes locale configuration with validation and memory allocation.

Algorithm:
1. Validate codePage parameter is within valid range [0, 5]
2. If codePage is invalid, return 0 (failure)
3. Acquire exclusive lock on locale resource (lock ID 0xc)
4. If configString is NULL: parse with default settings and return result
5. If configString is provided:
   a. Allocate 0x54-byte (84-byte) memory for new locale structure
   b. Parse and validate configuration via ParseAndApplyLocaleConfig
   c. If parse fails, return 0
   d. Initialize structure fields: clear reserved field, copy code pages
   e. Copy 6 locale-specific values from global array (loop 0-5)
   f. Copy validation state, variable-width mode flags
   g. Copy 7 locale table pointers (separators, monetary symbols, ctype)
   h. Check existing global locale: if non-NULL and not default, free it
   i. Update global thread-local locale pointer to new structure
   j. Invoke ___updatetlocinfo_lk() to update locale state
6. If parse failed and buffer allocated, free memory
7. Release locale lock
8. Return parse result (0=failure, nonzero=success)

Parameters:
codePage: Locale code page identifier (0=default, 1-5=specific locales)
pConfigString: Optional configuration string pointer (NULL=use default config)

Returns:
nonzero: Locale successfully initialized
0: Invalid code page, parse failed, or memory allocation failed

Special Cases:
Code page validation occurs before lock acquisition; invalid values skip all processing
configString can be NULL to initialize with default configuration
Allocated structure is 0x54 bytes containing 21 consecutive dword pointers
Thread-safe via critical section lock (lock ID 0xc)
Old locale structure freed only if exists and differs from default sentinel (0x6fc400d8)
Uses SEH exception handling for guaranteed cleanup on errors
Structure contains 21 pointers: reserved, activeCodePage, secondaryCodePage, 6 localeValues, validationState, variableWidthMode, 11 localeTablePointers

acquired during locale configuration. The lock protects concurrent access to locale structures
during initialization and modification.

- Ensures proper lock release regardless of initialization success or failure

0x6FBF7AE9.name: WriteCharToStream
0x6FBF7AE9.comment:
Writes a single character to a buffered file stream.

Algorithm:
1. Check if FILE structure has 0x40 flag set (no buffering flag) and base pointer is non-NULL
   If either condition fails, skip write and increment counter, then return
2. Decrement the buffer count (_cnt field at offset +0x4)
3. If count becomes negative, buffer is full: call __flsbuf to flush buffer
4. If count is still non-negative, write character to buffer:
   - Store AL (character) at current buffer pointer (_ptr field at offset +0x0)
   - Increment buffer pointer
   - Extend AL to 32-bit unsigned (MOVZX for zero-extension)
5. Check if write result is -1 (0xffffffff) indicating error
   If error, set output counter (ESI) to -1 and return
6. Otherwise increment output counter (*ESI) and return success

Parameters (IMPLICIT - Visual Studio __cdecl):
  AL: byte - Character to write to stream
  ECX: FILE* - Pointer to buffered file stream structure
  ESI: int* - Pointer to output character counter

Returns:
  No explicit return value. Updates ESI counter to -1 on error, increments on success.

Structure Layout:
FILE structure offsets:
  Offset 0x0: _ptr - pointer to current buffer position (char*)
  Offset 0x4: _cnt - remaining characters in buffer (int)
  Offset 0x8: _base - pointer to buffer base or NULL (char*)
  Offset 0xc: _flag - status flags including 0x40 (no-buffer flag) (int)

Special Cases:
  - 0x40 flag indicates unbuffered stream; no write performed
  - 0xffffffff return from __flsbuf indicates write failure (possibly disk full)
  - Negative count indicates buffer exhausted, requires flush
  - This is a Visual Studio C runtime library function for stream I/O

0x6FBF7B77.name: FormatStringProcessor
0x6FBF7B77.signature: void FormatStringProcessor(uint outputContext, byte * formatString, void * argList)
0x6FBF7B77.comment:
Printf-style format string processor - core formatting engine for vsprintf/vsnprintf

Algorithm:
1. Load and validate stack canary (XOR seed with frame pointer for overflow detection)
2. Initialize local buffers: character conversion buffer (467 bytes), wide char buffer, output state
3. Load first character from format string and enter main processing loop
4. While format string character is not null terminator:
   a) For regular ASCII characters (not %): output directly through WriteCharToStream callback
   b) For % character: reset format specification flags and enter state machine parser
   c) Parse format flags (-, +, space, #, 0) via lookup table until non-flag found
   d) Parse field width as decimal digits (or * to read width from va_list argument)
   e) Parse precision (.digits or .*) for string/float truncation and padding control
   f) Parse length modifiers (h for short, l for long, I64 for 64-bit, w for wide char)
   g) Parse conversion specifier and dispatch to type-specific handler (d,i,o,x,X,u,f,F,e,E,g,G,c,s,p,n)
5. Extract argument from va_list based on length modifier and pointer advancement
6. Convert argument to string representation:
   - Integers: use __aulldvrm for radix conversion (division loop), handles 32/64-bit signed/unsigned
   - Floats: call __cfltcvt with precision, use __forcdecpt for # flag, __cropzeros for g/G format
   - Strings: copy bytes/wide chars to buffer until null terminator, handle NULL pointer cases
   - Characters: convert single char or wide char using _wctomb if wide modifier set
   - Pointers: format as hex (base 16) with 0x prefix if # flag set
   - %n specifier: store character count output to pointer argument (short or int based on h flag)
7. Calculate padding requirements: compare field width against sign length and string length
8. Apply formatting to convert value to final output string:
   - Write leading space padding if left-align not set and no zero-pad flag
   - Write sign/prefix characters (+, -, space for numbers; 0x for hex)
   - Write zero padding if zero-pad flag set and not left-aligned
   - Write formatted string/number/character value
   - Write trailing space padding if left-align flag set
9. Output final formatted string through write_string/WriteCharRepeatCount callbacks
10. Loop to next format character and repeat until null terminator found
11. Perform stack canary validation: XOR canary with frame pointer again, call VerifyStackCanary
12. Return to caller (vsprintf/vsnprintf functions)

Parameters:
- outputContext: Opaque uint context passed to output callback functions (stream handle, buffer state, etc.)
- formatString: Null-terminated byte string containing printf format codes and literal characters
- argList: Pointer to va_list array containing arguments (each 4 or 8 bytes depending on conversion type)

Returns:
void - No direct return value; all output passed to registered callback functions

0x6FBF83B0.name: CopyString
0x6FBF83B0.comment:
Copies a null-terminated string from source to destination with 4-byte alignment optimization.

Algorithm:
1. Check source pointer alignment (lower 2 bits)
2. While source is not 4-byte aligned:
   - Copy one byte at a time
   - Check if byte is null terminator; if so, terminate
3. While source is 4-byte aligned:
   - Load 4 bytes from source
   - Use null-byte detection heuristic: (x ^ 0xffffffff ^ x + 0x7efefeff) & 0x81010100
   - If null byte found, determine which byte is null and copy only up to that byte
   - Otherwise, copy all 4 bytes
4. Return original destination pointer

Parameters:
- szDest: Destination buffer to write string into (char *)
- szSrc: Source string to copy from (char *)

Returns:
- szDest: Original destination pointer (unchanged)

Special Cases:
- Handles unaligned source pointers by byte-copying until aligned
- Uses efficient null-byte detection across 4-byte chunks
- Properly terminates at first null byte encountered
- Returns destination to support chaining (standard strcpy behavior)

0x6FBF83C0.name: StringConcatenate
0x6FBF83C0.comment:
Fast aligned string concatenation using null-byte detection.

Algorithm:
1. Align source pointer to 4-byte boundary while processing any unaligned prefix bytes
2. Find end of destination string using optimized word-wise null detection (magic constant 0x7efefeff)
3. Align source pointer to 4-byte boundary while copying prefix bytes from source
4. Process source in aligned 4-byte words using null-byte detection to find string terminator
5. Determine null position within final word (byte 0, 1, 2, or 3) and write appropriate data
6. Return pointer to destination string start

This implementation uses the standard null-byte detection pattern: (value XOR 0xffffffff XOR (value + 0x7efefeff)) AND 0x81010100 detects any null byte in a 32-bit word.

Parameters:
  pDestination: Pointer to destination buffer (null-terminated string where concatenation target resides)
  pSource: Pointer to source string to append (null-terminated)

Returns:

Special Cases:
  - Handles unaligned string pointers by processing byte-by-byte until 4-byte alignment
  - Uses word-wise operations for bulk copying once aligned
  - Correctly positions null terminator within final word based on null byte location

0x6FBF8644.signature: uint LocaleMapString(LCID localeId, DWORD mapFlags, LPCSTR sourceString, int sourceLength, LPSTR destString, int destLength, uint sourceCodePage, int mbszSourceFlag)
0x6FBF8644.comment:
Locale-aware string mapping and code page conversion function.

Algorithm:
1. Initialize locale capability cache (g_dwLocaleMapStringCapability):
   - If not cached, test LCMapStringW with flag 0x100 on test string
   - Cache result: 1 for success (wide-char path), 2 for failure (direct mapping)
   - On error 0x78, force direct mapping mode
2. Calculate actual source string length by scanning for null terminator if needed
3. Branch on cached capability and select mapping path:
   Path A (Capability=1, wide-char path):
   - Allocate temporary wide-char buffer (size: wideCharCount*2 rounded to DWORD)
   - Convert source ANSI to wide chars using MultiByteToWideChar
   - Map wide string using LCMapStringW with provided mapFlags
   - If mapFlags & 0x400: Direct wide output, else convert back to ANSI
   - Allocate second wide buffer if output conversion needed
   - Convert mapped result to ANSI using WideCharToMultiByte
   - Free temporary buffers on exit
   Path B (Capability=0 or 2, direct mapping):
   - Use default locale (g_dwDefaultLocaleId) if localeId is 0
   - Get default code page from g_dwActiveCodePage if sourceCodePage is 0
   - Query target code page for locale using GetLocaleDefaultCodePage
   - If code pages match: call LCMapStringA directly
   - If code pages differ: transcode source using ConvertCodePageString
   - Map transcoded string with LCMapStringA
   - Convert result back to source code page using ConvertCodePageString
   - Free all intermediate buffers
4. Return character count written (or 0 on any allocation/conversion failure)

Parameters:
  localeId (LCID): Locale identifier for string operations (0 = use default)
  mapFlags (DWORD): LC_MAP_* flags for transformation (0x400 = skip output conversion)

0x6FBF8BBD.name: ReallocateMemory
0x6FBF8BBD.comment:
Reallocates a memory block to a new size using the system heap.

Algorithm:
1. Acquire critical section lock (critical section 4)
2. If pOriginalBlock is NULL, allocate new block with newSize and return
3. If newSize is 0, free original block and return NULL
4. If heap state is not initialized (g_dwHeapState != 3), attempt error recovery with low memory handling
5. If newSize is small (less than 32 bytes), use small block allocator path:
   a. Try in-place resize with ___sbh_resize_block
   b. If resize fails, allocate new block and copy data using _memcpy
   c. Free original block after successful copy
6. For larger blocks (32+ bytes), use heap allocator:
   a. Align size to 16-byte boundary (add 15, AND with 0xFFFFFFF0)
   b. Call g_pfnHeapAlloc (HeapAlloc) to allocate new block
   c. Copy original data up to min(originalSize, newSize) bytes
   d. Free original block using ___sbh_free_block
7. If allocation fails and low memory flag set, invoke memory pressure callback and retry allocation
8. Release critical section lock and return allocated block pointer (or NULL on failure)

Parameters:
- pOriginalBlock (EDI): Pointer to existing memory block to reallocate, or NULL for new allocation
- newSize (ESI): Requested size in bytes for reallocated block

Returns:

Structure Layout:
- Block header (offset -4): Contains original size - 1 (used by resize operations)
- Block data (offset 0): User-accessible data payload

Special Cases:
- If newSize is 0, block is freed and NULL is returned
- If pOriginalBlock is NULL, newSize bytes are allocated as new block
- Small blocks (< 32 bytes) use specialized small block heap allocator
- Large blocks use system HeapAlloc/HeapReAlloc
- Alignment: All allocations aligned to 16-byte boundary
- Low memory handling: If allocation fails with low memory condition set, retry after cleanup callback
- Lock: Critical section 4 held throughout operation to serialize heap access

0x6FBF9198.name: AllocateMemory
0x6FBF9198.comment:
Allocates a zero-initialized memory block for element arrays with automatic retry on failure.

Algorithm:
1. Validate parameters: elementCount must be non-zero AND elementSize must be <= 0xffffffe0 / elementCount to prevent integer overflow
2. Calculate total allocation size by multiplying elementCount * elementSize
3. If calculated size is zero, set minimum allocation to 1 byte (handles edge case of zero-sized requests)
4. Enter allocation loop with two strategies based on heap configuration:
   a. Small Block Heap (SBH) optimization: If g_dwHeapState == 3 AND original size <= g_dwMaxSmallBlockSize:
      - Align size to 16-byte boundary (size + 0xF AND 0xFFFFFFF0) for SBH alignment requirements
      - Acquire critical section lock (index 4) for thread-safe SBH access
      - Call ___sbh_alloc_block with original (unaligned) size to allocate from small block heap
      - Release critical section lock
      - If allocation succeeds: Zero-initialize memory with memset and return pointer
   b. Windows HeapAlloc fallback: Call HeapAlloc with HEAP_ZERO_MEMORY flag (0x8) to allocate from process heap and zero-initialize
5. Test allocation result: If non-NULL, return allocated pointer immediately
6. Test out-of-memory handler flag (g_dwLowMemoryFlag): If zero, return NULL (no recovery possible)
7. Call __callnewh handler to attempt memory recovery (e.g., purge caches, free resources)
8. If handler returns non-zero, loop back to step 4 to retry allocation; otherwise fall through to failure
9. Return NULL if allocation fails and handler returns zero (no recovery possible)

Parameters:
elementCount - uint: Number of elements to allocate (multiplied with elementSize to determine total bytes)
elementSize - uint: Size in bytes of each individual element

Returns:
int * : Pointer to allocated and zero-initialized memory block on success
        NULL (0x00000000) if allocation fails persistently or parameters cause integer overflow

Special Cases:
- Zero-size requests: If elementCount * elementSize == 0, minimum 1-byte allocation is attempted
- Integer overflow protection: DIV instruction at 0x6fbf91b0 compares product against 0xffffffe0 limit to detect overflow
- SBH optimization: Allocations <= g_dwMaxSmallBlockSize use aligned small block heap for better fragmentation behavior
- Size alignment: SBH allocations aligned to 16-byte boundary; heap allocations use HEAP_ZERO_MEMORY flag
- Retry mechanism: __callnewh handler called on allocation failure to attempt memory recovery before final failure
- Heap handles and state: Uses g_pHeapHandle (process heap handle), g_dwHeapState (mode), g_dwMaxSmallBlockSize (SBH threshold)

Global Data References:
g_pHeapHandle (0x6fc47b94) - Handle to process heap for Windows HeapAlloc calls
g_dwHeapState (0x6fc47b98) - Heap mode flag (value 3 enables small block heap optimization)
g_dwMaxSmallBlockSize (0x6fc46910) - Maximum size threshold for small block heap allocations
g_dwLowMemoryFlag (0x6fc427c4) - Flag indicating if out-of-memory handler should be invoked

2. Test if driveNumber is 0 (current drive case)
3. If driveNumber == 0: Call GetCurrentDirectoryA(0x104, pathResultBuffer)
4. If driveNumber != 0:
   a. Validate drive using __validdrive(driveNumber)
   b. If validation fails (return == 0), set error codes 0xf and 0xd, jump to cleanup
   c. If valid: Format drive string as "D:." (e.g., "C:.") in driveString buffer
   d. Call GetFullPathNameA(driveString, 0x104, pathResultBuffer, &filenamePart)
5. Check if GetCurrentDirectoryA/GetFullPathNameA returned valid length (non-zero)
6. Calculate requiredSize = pathLength + 1 (for null terminator)
7. Verify requiredSize does not exceed 0x105 (261 bytes including terminator)
8. Test if pathBuffer was provided (NULL vs non-NULL pointer)
9. If pathBuffer == NULL:
   a. Compare requiredSize against bufferSize parameter
   b. Use larger of the two values as allocation size
   c. Call _malloc(requiredSize) to allocate buffer
   d. If malloc returns NULL, set error 0xc (ENOMEM) and return
10. If pathBuffer != NULL:
    a. Compare requiredSize against provided bufferSize
    b. If requiredSize > bufferSize, set error 0x22 (EINVAL) and return
11. Call CopyString(pathBuffer, pathResultBuffer) to copy result to output buffer
12. Verify stack canary integrity using VerifyStackCanary(stackCanary XOR EBP)
13. Return pointer to path buffer in EAX (or NULL if errors occurred)

    0x22 = EINVAL (Invalid argument, buffer too small)

0x6FBFAC37.name: InitializeLocaleCharacterClassification
0x6FBFAC37.comment:
Initializes locale-specific character classification tables for multi-byte string processing.

Algorithm:
1. Check if initialization flag (g_dwDefaultLocaleId) is set; use default table if so
2. Check if code page ID already cached in g_dwActiveCodePage; if not, detect it
3. Allocate three temporary buffers: 4-byte ref count, 768-byte char type table, 257-byte lookup table
4. Initialize lookup table with sequential byte values (0x00-0x0FF) for identity mapping
5. Call GetCPInfo to retrieve code page lead byte ranges (for multi-byte code pages)
6. Store max character width from code page info in g_dwVariableWidthModeEnabled
7. For multi-byte code pages with lead bytes: mark lead byte ranges in lookup table with 0x00
8. Call ___crtGetStringTypeA to classify all 256 characters into character type flags
9. Clear terminator flag at offset 0x0FE in character type table (lead byte end marker)
10. For multi-byte code pages: set 0x8000 flag on all lead byte character type entries
11. Copy processed character type data (0x0FE bytes) from offset 0x200 to offset 0x100
12. Store pointers: g_pCTypeTablePtr = char type table, g_dwLocalePositiveSignTable = terminator, g_dwLocaleNegativeSignTable = ref count
13. Free temporary lookup table; other buffers remain allocated
14. Verify stack canary and return

Parameters:
None (uses global variables: g_dwDefaultLocaleId, g_dwActiveCodePage, g_wDefaultLocaleId)

Returns:
void

Special Cases:
- If g_dwDefaultLocaleId set: skips all processing and uses default table at g_szDefaultCharacterTypeTable
- If memory allocation fails: cleans up partial allocations and returns
- If GetCPInfo fails or max character size > 5: aborts with cleanup
- Single-byte code pages (MaxCharSize == 1): skip all lead byte processing
- Multi-byte code pages with no lead bytes: skip lead byte marking
- Character type table uses 2-byte stride (WORD entries) for classification flags

Data Structures:
The function allocates and processes a 0x300-byte (768-byte) character table with structure:
- Offset 0x000-0x0FF: Lookup table - input character mapping (1-byte entries)
- Offset 0x100-0x1FF: Character type flags - output classification (2-byte WORD entries)
- Offset 0x200-0x2FF: Scratch space for string type data
Each character's classification stored as WORD with bit flags:
- 0x8000: Lead byte marker (first byte of multi-byte sequence)
- Other bits: Character type flags from system GetStringTypeA call

0x6FBFB3C7.name: GetCountryCodePage
0x6FBFB3C7.comment:
Converts country/locale code string to numeric Windows code page value

Algorithm:
1. Load stack guard seed from g_dwStackGuardSeed global and XOR with stack address for canary validation
2. Check if szCountryCode parameter is NULL or empty string; if so jump to use default locale type
3. Compare szCountryCode string against szLocaleStringACP ("ACP") for exact match
4. If ACP match found, set dwLocaleType to 0x1004 (default country code request)
5. Compare szCountryCode against szLocaleStringOCP ("OCP") for exact match
6. If OCP match found, set dwLocaleType to 0xb (specific locale request); otherwise buffer passed through
7. Call g_pfnGetLocaleInfoA with g_pCurrentLocaleHandle, dwLocaleType, and 8-byte abLocaleBuffer
8. If GetLocaleInfoA returns zero (failure), skip conversion and jump to canary verification
9. Convert returned locale string from abLocaleBuffer to numeric value using _atol
10. Verify stack canary XOR value to detect buffer overflow before returning result to caller

Parameters:
szCountryCode: Pointer to null-terminated country/locale code string (passed in ECX register by __fastcall)

Returns:
Numeric code page value on successful GetLocaleInfoA call; 0 on GetLocaleInfoA failure

Special Cases:
- NULL or empty input triggers default locale request with dwLocaleType 0x1004
- szLocaleStringACP ("ACP") triggers default type 0x1004 for Active Code Page
- szLocaleStringOCP ("OCP") triggers specific type 0xb for OEM Code Page
- Unknown country codes are passed through directly as-is to GetLocaleInfoA
- 8-byte abLocaleBuffer limits string length to 7 characters plus null terminator
- Stack canary verification detects buffer overruns before return to caller

0x6FBFB441.name: FindValueInLocaleList
0x6FBFB441.comment:
Searches for a given short value within a fixed 10-element locale code list.

Algorithm:
1. Initialize search offset to 0
2. Load the search value parameter into CX register
3. Compare search value against word at g_wLocaleCodeList[offset]
4. If match found, return success (0)
5. Increment offset by 2 bytes (size of short)
6. If offset < 20 bytes (10 shorts), repeat from step 3
7. Return failure (1) if no match found after full list scan

Parameters:
- searchValue: Short value to locate in the locale code list

Returns:
- 0 (EAX) if value is found in the list
- 1 (EAX) if value is not found in the list

Special Cases:
- The list contains exactly 10 short values (20 bytes total)
- List address is fixed at 0x6fc3487c
- Search uses linear scan, O(n) complexity
- Search terminates immediately on first match

0x6FBFB45F.name: GetLocaleInfoWithCache
0x6FBFB45F.signature: int GetLocaleInfoWithCache(uint dwLocaleId, LCTYPE lcType, char * szBuffer, int nBufferSize)
0x6FBFB45F.comment:
Retrieves locale-specific information from cached locale table with Win32 fallback.

Algorithm:
1. Initialize binary search bounds: searchLow = 0, searchHigh = 26
2. Perform binary search on g_dwLocaleIdTable array indexed by locale ID
3. For each iteration, calculate midIndex and fetch locale ID at that position
4. Compare target localeId with fetched value; adjust bounds based on comparison
5. When locale found, dispatch based on lcType parameter to retrieve appropriate data:
   - lcType 1: Return decimal separator from g_szDecimalSeparatorTable
   - lcType 3: Return thousands separator from g_szThousandsSeparatorTable
   - lcType 7: Return list separator from g_szListSeparatorTable
   - lcType 11 (0xB): Return monetary decimal from g_szMonetaryDecimalTable
   - lcType 4097 (0x1001): Return grouping pattern pointer from g_pszGroupingTable
   - lcType 4098 (0x1002): Return monetary grouping pointer from g_pszMonGroupingTable
   - lcType 4100 (0x1004): Return decimal grouping from g_szDecimalGroupingTable
6. If locale data found and buffer valid (size > 0), copy data with null termination
7. If locale not found or invalid data, fall back to Win32 GetLocaleInfoA API
8. Return 1 on success, Win32 result on fallback

Parameters:
  localeId (uint): Windows locale identifier to search for in locale table
  lcType (LCTYPE): Locale information type constant (1, 3, 7, 11, 0x1001, 0x1002, 0x1004)
  pBuffer (char *): Destination buffer for locale information string
  bufferSize (int): Size of destination buffer in bytes (minimum 1 for null terminator)

Returns:
  int: 1 if data found in cache and copied successfully, or Win32 GetLocaleInfoA result
       if locale not in cache or on error

Special Cases:
  - Binary search stride of 0x2C (44 bytes) per locale entry
  - Stride magic: 0x2C = 44 bytes (size of one locale table entry structure)
  - Buffer size validation: Returns 0 if bufferSize < 1
  - String data copied with (bufferSize - 1) to ensure null termination
  - Fallback uses indirect call through g_pfnGetLocaleInfoA function pointer

0x6FBFB62C.name: ValidateLocaleIdFromHexResource
0x6FBFB62C.comment:
Validates a locale ID by converting it from a hex-encoded string resource and comparing it with the input parameter. Used for locale configuration verification in resource-based locale setup.

Algorithm:
1. Initialize security stack canary (XOR with EBP base) stored at [EBP-0x4]
2. Build resource ID by masking input localeId with 0x3FF and ORing with 0x400 to create lookup key
3. Load resource string using g_pfnGetLocaleInfoA (function pointer at 0x6fc4276c) with buffer size 0x78 into szLocaleHexBuffer [EBP-0x7c]
4. Test resource load result - if zero (resource not found), jump to resource_load_failed and return success (0) to allow graceful degradation
5. Call _LcidFromHexString to convert the hex-encoded string to a locale ID
6. Compare converted locale ID (EAX) with input localeId parameter [EBP+0x8]
7. If IDs match, jump to id_match_success and proceed to canary verification
8. If IDs mismatch and validationRequired [EBP+0xc] is zero, jump to validation_disabled_exit
9. If validation required, call _strlen on global string g_szLocaleValidationFormat (0x6fc42768) to get length
10. Call _GetPrimaryLen to get language-specific substring length and compare with _strlen result
11. If lengths mismatch, set EAX=1 and exit with failure status
12. If all validations pass, set EAX=0 for success
13. Verify stack canary integrity (XOR with EBP) and return result

Parameters:
  localeId (uint) - Locale ID to validate, masked with 0x3FF and OR'd with 0x400 for resource table lookup
  validationRequired (int) - Validation flag: 0 = skip detailed validation, non-zero = perform full validation

Returns:
  int - 0 on success (validation passed or resource not found or validation not required), 1 on failure (validation failed)

Special Cases:
  - Resource load failure (nResourceLoadResult == 0) returns success (0) to support graceful degradation when locale resources are unavailable
  - Stack guard canary at [EBP-0x4] protects against buffer overflows in szLocaleHexBuffer (120 bytes at [EBP-0x7c])
  - validationRequired=0 allows early exit on ID mismatch without string length comparison
  - Magic mask 0x3FF limits locale ID to 10-bit range, 0x400 sets bit 10 to select resource table section
  - _GetPrimaryLen may return different result than _strlen for non-ASCII locale strings due to language-specific handling

0x6FBFB6A1.name: ProcessLocaleHexString
0x6FBFB6A1.signature: uint ProcessLocaleHexString(void * this, void * pThis, char * pHexLocaleString)
0x6FBFB6A1.comment:
Processes a hexadecimal locale identifier and validates/configures three locale states.

Algorithm:
1. Initialize stack canary (EBP-4) by XORing seed with stack address
2. Convert input hex locale string to numeric locale ID
3. Query first locale property (0x1002 or 0xFFFFF005 conditional) into 120-byte buffer
4. If query fails, clear all config flags (0) and exit
5. Compare first result against g_szLocaleConfigString using case-insensitive comparison
6. If first property matches:
   a. Query second property (0x1001 or 0xFFFFF002 conditional)
   b. Compare against g_szLocaleValidationFormat
   c. If both match, set flags 0x304 (bits 2,8,9), store in g_dwPrimaryLocaleId
   d. If only first matches and flag 0x2 not set:
      - If substring length available, compare using g_dwLocaleStringLength limit
      - If substring matches, set flag 0x2, store in g_dwTertiaryLocaleId
      - If full length matches g_dwLocaleStringLength, also store in g_dwPrimaryLocaleId
      - Else search for locale ID in validation list via FindValueInLocaleList()
      - If found in list and flag 0x1 not set, set flag 0x1, store in g_dwTertiaryLocaleId
7. If both flags 0x300 set (bits 8,9), skip to canary check and exit
8. Query third property (0x1001 or 0xFFFFF002 conditional)
9. If query fails, clear flags and exit
10. Compare third result against g_szLocaleValidationFormat
11. If exact match found:
    - Set flag 0x200 (bit 9 high byte)
    - If secondary config unset and length limit set, verify full length match
    - If full match, call ValidateLocaleIdFromHexResource(localeId, 1)
    - Else exit without further validation
12. Else (mismatch):
    - If secondary config set or no length limit, exit
    - Else perform substring comparison using length limit
    - If substring matches, call ValidateLocaleIdFromHexResource(localeId, 0)
13. If validation succeeds, set flag 0x100 (bit 8 low byte)
14. If g_dwPrimaryLocaleId unset, store current locale ID there
15. Verify stack canary before return to detect buffer overflow

Parameters:
pThis (ECX - implicit): Context/this pointer for locale object
pHexLocaleString (EDX): Pointer to hex string to convert to locale ID

Returns:
EAX: Status code computed as (~(flags >> 2)) & 1
     Returns 1 if flag 0x2 not set, 0 if flag 0x2 is set

Special Cases:
- Flag bits tracked in g_dwLocaleConfigFlags: bit 0=0x1 (alternate), bit 1=0x2 (secondary), bits 8-9=0x300 (primary/tertiary)
- Three locale ID storage: g_dwPrimaryLocaleId, g_dwTertiaryLocaleId, g_dwSecondaryLocaleId
- Property queries use conditional flag bits (0xFFFFF005 or 0xFFFFF002) based on g_pSecondaryLocaleConfig state
- Stack canary validates against seed from g_dwStackGuardSeed to detect overflow
- Maximum buffer size: 120 bytes (0x78) for locale info queries
- Hex string conversion via _LcidFromHexString() function pointer

0x6FBFB8BF.name: ValidateAndApplyLocaleFromHexString
0x6FBFB8BF.signature: void ValidateAndApplyLocaleFromHexString(void * this, void * pThis, char * pszHexLocaleString)
0x6FBFB8BF.comment:
Validates and applies a locale ID from hexadecimal string representation

Algorithm:
1. Verify stack canary guard value using XOR with frame pointer
2. Convert hex string parameter to numeric locale ID via _LcidFromHexString
3. Compute locale info flags: if g_dwSecondaryLocaleId != 0 then 0xfffff002 + 0x1001 else 0x1001
4. Fetch locale display name using function pointer g_pfnGetLocaleInfoA with locale ID, flags, and 120-byte buffer
5. Check if locale name fetch succeeded (non-zero return indicates success)
6. Perform case-insensitive comparison with reference name (g_szLocaleValidationFormat)
7. If exact match AND g_dwSecondaryLocaleId == 0: Set matchType = 1 for exact validation
8. If no exact match AND g_dwSecondaryLocaleId == 0 AND g_dwLocaleStringLength != 0: Perform substring comparison
9. Call ValidateLocaleIdFromHexResource with locale ID and matchType parameter
10. On validation success: OR g_dwLocaleConfigFlags with 0x4 and store locale ID to primary and tertiary locations
11. Verify stack canary before return

Parameters:
- pThis: void* - Implicit 'this' pointer for object context
- pszHexLocaleString: char* - Null-terminated hex string representation of locale ID to validate

Returns:
- void - No explicit return value. On success, modifies globals: g_dwLocaleConfigFlags, g_dwPrimaryLocaleId, g_dwTertiaryLocaleId

Special Cases:
- Magic number 0x78 (120): Size of locale name buffer for API call
- Magic number 0x4: Bit flag OR'd into g_dwLocaleConfigFlags on successful validation
- Magic number 0xfffff002 + 0x1001: Computed flags when g_dwSecondaryLocaleId is non-zero
- If fetch fails (returns 0): Clears g_dwLocaleConfigFlags and exits without further processing
- Partial match allowed only when g_dwSecondaryLocaleId == 0 and g_dwLocaleStringLength is non-zero

0x6FBFC0AA.name: InitializeLocaleCharacterMaps
0x6FBFC0AA.comment:
Initializes locale-specific character case mapping tables and character class flags.

Algorithm:
1. Initialize stack canary for buffer overflow protection using XOR with global seed
2. Call GetCPInfo to retrieve code page information for current locale
3. If code page info available (locale-aware path):
   a. Create character table (0-255) with space as default for index 0
   b. Process lead byte ranges from cpInfo.LeadByte to mark multi-byte characters
   c. Fill all lead byte range positions with spaces (0x20)
   d. Call ___crtGetStringTypeA to retrieve character type information (CT_CTYPE1)
   e. Call LocaleMapString with LCMAP_UPPERCASE to build uppercase conversion table
   f. Call LocaleMapString with LCMAP_LOWERCASE to build lowercase conversion table
   g. For each character 0-255:
      - If character is alphanumeric (CT_CTYPE1 & 0x01):
        * Set bit 0x10 (uppercase flag) in DAT_6fc47960[i+1]
        * Copy uppercase mapping from uppercaseMap to DAT_6fc47a80[i]
      - Else if character is lowercase (CT_CTYPE1 & 0x02):
        * Set bit 0x20 (lowercase flag) in DAT_6fc47960[i+1]
        * Copy lowercase mapping from lowercaseMap to DAT_6fc47a80[i]
      - Else set DAT_6fc47a80[i] to 0 (no mapping)
4. If code page info unavailable (ASCII fallback path):
   a. For each character 0-255:
      - If character is A-Z (0x41-0x5A):
        * Set bit 0x10 (uppercase) in DAT_6fc47960[i+1]
        * Convert to lowercase by adding 0x20, store in DAT_6fc47a80[i]
      - Else if character is a-z (0x61-0x7A):
        * Set bit 0x20 (lowercase) in DAT_6fc47960[i+1]
        * Convert to uppercase by subtracting 0x20, store in DAT_6fc47a80[i]
      - Else set DAT_6fc47a80[i] to 0 (non-alphabetic)
5. Verify stack canary integrity and return

Returns: void - Populates global character mapping tables as side effect

Special Cases:
- DAT_6fc406bc: Global XOR seed for stack canary
- DAT_6fc47a64: Current code page identifier
- DAT_6fc47944: Locale handle
- DAT_6fc47960: Character class flags (-1 offset for 1-based indexing)
- DAT_6fc47a80: Character case mapping table output
- Lead byte handling: Multi-byte character encodings skip uppercase mapping
- Fallback mode: Basic ASCII-only conversion used if GetCPInfo fails

Character Class Flags (DAT_6fc47960):
- 0x10: Uppercase character
- 0x20: Lowercase character
- 0x00: Non-alphabetic or unmapped

0x6FBFC245.name: SetupCodePage
0x6FBFC245.comment:
SetupCodePage - Initialize locale character classification maps for a specific code page
This function configures the runtime character classification tables (upper/lower case, digits, whitespace, etc.)
for the specified code page. It either uses predefined tables for known code pages or retrieves them
from the system via GetCPInfo API. The character type bitmap is stored in a global 256-entry table
where each byte represents the character types for that code point.

Algorithm:
1. Initialize stack canary for buffer overflow detection
2. Check if codePage parameter is non-zero; if zero, use default SBCS setup
3. Search predefined code page table (8 entries) for matching code page ID
4. If found in predefined list:
   a. Clear the global character type table (DAT_6fc47960, 256 bytes)
   b. For each of 4 lead byte ranges in predefined table:
      i. Iterate through range start/end pairs
      ii. Mark bytes in range with 0x4 flag (lead byte indicator)
   c. Mark all single-byte values 0x01-0xFE with 0x8 flag (trail byte indicator)
5. If not found, call GetCPInfo to retrieve system code page information
6. If GetCPInfo succeeds:
   a. Clear character type table

      ii. Mark each byte in range with 0x4 flag
      iii. Mark all single bytes 0x01-0xFE with 0x8 flag

8. Store code page ID in DAT_6fc47a64

10. Verify stack canary and return

Parameters:
codePage - Requested code page identifier (0 = use default, >0 = specific code page to configure)

Returns:
void - Configuration stored in global character classification tables

Special Cases:
- Code page 0 uses default SBCS (Single-Byte Character Set) setup
- Predefined code pages use static tables, reducing system calls
- Lead byte ranges marked with 0x04 flag, trail bytes with 0x08 flag
- Maximum of 8 predefined code pages; beyond that uses GetCPInfo
- Character type table DAT_6fc47960 is 256 bytes (one entry per possible byte value)

0x6FBFC642.name: UnlockFileHandle
0x6FBFC642.comment:
Wrapper function to unlock a file handle with implicit register parameter.

This is a CRT utility function that provides a thin wrapper around __unlock_fhandle.
The function preserves the EBX register which contains the file handle context that
needs to be unlocked. This unusual calling pattern is used to pass the file handle
as an implicit parameter via EBX rather than through the standard stack.

Algorithm:
1. PUSH EBX - Save the file handle (implicit parameter) on stack
2. CALL __unlock_fhandle - Call the unlocking function with EBX preserved
3. POP ECX - Pop return address into ECX (discards saved EBX semantically)
4. RET - Return to caller

Parameters:
IMPLICIT (EBX): File handle context to unlock. The EBX register contains the
                file handle that should be unlocked by __unlock_fhandle.

Returns:
void - No explicit return value. The function performs file handle cleanup as
       a side effect of calling __unlock_fhandle.

Special Cases:
- The PUSH/POP pattern is unusual but necessary to preserve EBX while calling
  __unlock_fhandle which expects EBX to contain the file handle.
- Called exclusively from __lseek error handling paths to ensure file handles
  are properly unlocked when seek operations fail.
- This is part of the C Runtime file I/O implementation for proper resource cleanup.

0x6FBFC666.name: WriteFileWithTextModeConversion
0x6FBFC666.signature: int WriteFileWithTextModeConversion(uint dwFileDescriptor, char * szBuffer, uint dwBytesToWrite)
0x6FBFC666.comment:
Writes data to a file descriptor with text mode CRLF conversion.

Algorithm:
1. Initialize canary value for stack overflow detection
2. Return 0 if bytesToWrite is 0
3. Locate file entry in global descriptor table using descriptor index
4. Check EOF mode flag (0x20): seek to end of file if set
5. Check binary mode flag (0x80):
   a. If binary mode (flag clear): call WriteFile directly and return result
   b. If text mode (flag set): convert LF to CRLF before writing
6. Text mode conversion loop:
   a. Initialize input position and conversion buffer
   b. For each byte in input buffer:
      - If byte is LF (0x0a): insert CR (0x0d) and increment newline count
      - Store byte in conversion buffer
   c. When buffer reaches 1024 bytes or input exhausted: call WriteFile
   d. Verify all converted data was written
   e. Continue until entire input buffer processed
7. Handle WriteFile errors: map Windows error codes to DOS error numbers
8. Final validation: check special flags and Ctrl-Z marker (0x1a)
9. Return total bytes written minus newline count for text mode

Parameters:
  fileDescriptor (ECX): Index into global file descriptor table
  pBuffer (EDI): Pointer to data to write
  bytesToWrite (ESP+0x3b4): Number of bytes to write

Returns:
  EAX: On success, returns bytes written (excluding inserted CRs)
       On error, returns -1 (0xffffffff)
       Special case: returns bytes_written - newline_count for text mode

Special Cases:
  - Text mode: Each LF becomes CRLF, increasing byte count written by newline count
  - File mode 0x80: Indicates text mode conversion needed
  - File mode 0x20: Indicates EOF mode, triggers seek to end
  - File mode 0x40: Special flag affecting final validation
  - Error code 5: Mapped to special handling with errno 9 and 5
  - Ctrl-Z (0x1a) with 0x40 flag: Suppresses error reporting
  - Chunking: 1024-byte (0x400) conversion buffer for efficient processing

Structure Layout:
File descriptor entry structure (36 bytes per entry):
  Offset Size Field Name         Type        Description
  +0x00   4    hFileHandle        HANDLE      Windows file handle
  +0x04   1    dwFileMode         byte        File mode flags (0x20=EOF, 0x40=special, 0x80=text)
  +0x05+  31   reserved           byte[31]    Reserved fields

3a. If within custom lock range: calculate array index by subtracting base address and shifting right 5 bits (dividing by 32), add 0x10 offset, call __lock with calculated index
3b. If outside custom range: treat as CRITICAL_SECTION pointer, add 0x20 offset for structure field, call EnterCriticalSection
4. Return from function

0x6FBFCA27.name: AcquireStreamLock

Algorithm:
1. Load streamIndex parameter from stack [ESP + 0x4]
2. Compare streamIndex against threshold 0x14 (20 decimal)
3. If streamIndex < 0x14: Add 0x10 offset and call __lock() (fast path)
4. If streamIndex >= 0x14: Load FILE pointer, add 0x20 offset to CRITICAL_SECTION, call EnterCriticalSection() (critical section path)

pFileStream (FILE*) - Pointer to FILE structure with CRITICAL_SECTION at offset +0x20
