0x6FC02D40.name: InitializePlayerUnitData
0x6FC02D40.comment:
Initializes a player unit with configuration data from a config structure.

Algorithm:
1. Extract player data pointer and slot index from pPlayerConfig structure
2. Determine position array: if slot index matches data structure slot, use pPlayerConfig[0] as position array, else find unit via FindUnitByDataCompare and clear message queues
3. Retrieve/initialize unit pointer via FindUnitByDataCompare
4. Initialize template unit (attribute reference) via InitializeGameUnit
5. Validate both unit pointers are non-null; if either is null, skip to config storage
6. Mark current unit slot as inactive via MarkUnitSlotInactive
7. Copy stat/attribute data to unit offset +0x118 from pPlayerConfig[+0xc]
8. Copy configuration DWORD to unit offset +0x200 from pPlayerConfig[+0x8]
9. Copy player level (WORD) to unit offsets +0x1d8 and +0x1e2 from pPlayerConfig[+0x10]
10. Load template unit level from offset +0x1d0 and store to unit offset +0x1d0
11. Compare player level with template level; if different and difference < 0x7fff, set flag 0x4 at unit offset +0x118
12. Copy position data (4 DWORDs) from position array to unit offsets +0x108-+0x11c
13. Copy 128-byte inventory from pPlayerConfig[+0x24] to unit offset +0x8 via CopyMemoryAndDetectTerminator
14. Calculate secondary inventory offset using CalculateStringLength
15. Copy 128-byte secondary inventory to unit offset +0x88
16. Store player configuration via StorePlayerSlotData
17. Process message queue 1: iterate through linked list at template unit offset +0x1c8, process nodes where level difference < 0x8000
18. Process message queue 2: iterate through linked list at template unit offset +0x180, process nodes where level difference < 0x8000
19. Check if event notifications enabled (g_byUnitProcessingEnabled != 0xff); if enabled and unit valid and flag 0x4 not set, create user event node

Parameters:
pPlayerConfig (uint*): Pointer to player initialization structure containing configuration data at various offsets

Returns:
void (no return value)

Special Cases:
- If unit pointer or template pointer is null, skips unit field initialization and proceeds directly to config storage
- Level difference calculated as (playerLevel - templateLevel) using unsigned 16-bit arithmetic
- Message queues only process nodes where unsigned(level_diff) < 0x8000 to filter by level range
- Event notification creation stores event type 0x2 at offset +0x8 and player slot ID at offset +0xc
- Both message queue processing loops handle null/invalid node pointers gracefully

Structure Layout:
Player Config Structure:
Offset | Size | Field Name | Type | Purpose
0x00   | 4    | pPositionArray | uint* | Position data (4 DWORDs: x, y, z, extra)
0x04   | 4    | dwSlotOrCompareVal | uint | Unit slot index or comparison value
0x08   | 4    | dwConfig | uint | Unit configuration data
0x0c   | 4    | dwStatAttribute | uint | Stat/attribute value (stored at unit +0x118)
0x10   | 2    | wPlayerLevel | word | Player level for unit initialization
0x24   | 128  | byInventoryData | byte[128] | Inventory data buffer

0x6FC02F00.name: UpdateUnitSkillCooldownThreshold
0x6FC02F00.comment:
Updates skill cooldown thresholds for a unit by comparing elapsed time against max cooldown.

Algorithm:
1. Dereference input pointer to get unit data value
2. Locate unit in game memory using FindUnitByDataCompare
3. Call GetTickCount to retrieve current system time
4. If unit not found, exit without changes
5. Calculate elapsed time: current_tick - unit.lastSkillTime
6. Store elapsed time in unit.currentCooldown field (+0x128)
7. Compare max cooldown threshold (unit.maxThreshold at +0x12c) against elapsed time
8. If max_threshold > elapsed: update max_threshold to elapsed value
9. Store updated max_threshold back to unit structure
10. Return with stack cleanup

Parameters:
  pUnit: Pointer to unit data value for lookup (passed to FindUnitByDataCompare)

Returns:
  void (modifies unit structure in-place)

Structure Layout (UnitAny offsets):
  +0x124: lastSkillTime (DWORD) - timestamp of last skill activation
  +0x128: currentCooldown (DWORD) - elapsed time since last skill
  +0x12c: maxThreshold (DWORD) - maximum cooldown threshold

Special Cases:
  - If FindUnitByDataCompare returns NULL, function exits immediately without modifications
  - Cooldown threshold capped at maximum value observed during function execution
  - Uses GetTickCount for time measurement (32-bit millisecond counter)

0x6FC02F40.name: BuildNetworkMessagePacket
0x6FC02F40.signature: uint * BuildNetworkMessagePacket(byte byPlayerIndex, char chMessageType, uint * payloadData, uint dwPayloadSize)
0x6FC02F40.comment:
Constructs a network message packet with header and payload data for transmission to remote players.

Algorithm:
1. Initialize game unit context to determine local player reference
2. Allocate 16-byte header buffer for player/unit context data
3. Calculate aligned message buffer size (minimum 4 bytes, aligned to dword boundary)
4. Allocate message buffer and copy player context from offset +0x108 (unit fields 0x42-0x45)
5. Populate message header: player index (+0x8), message type (+0x9), unit flags (+0xa)
6. Apply special case for server messages (playerIndex==0 && messageType==0x01): set sequence to 0
7. Otherwise load sequence counter from unit at offset [EBX + playerIndex*2 + 0x1cc] and increment
8. Copy payload data to message buffer offset +0x0c using dword copy + byte remainder loop
9. Calculate CRC16 checksum via CalculateBufferChecksum() and store at message header offset +0x00
10. Create exception frame node for network transmission (offset context varies by local vs remote)
11. Populate frame node: header pointer (+0x8), message pointer (+0xc), total size (+0x10), flags (+0x14)
12. Store current tick count from GetTickCount() into frame node (+0x18)
13. Update global packet statistics (g_dwPacketBytesTransmitted) if remote player
14. Return frame node pointer or null if frame allocation fails

Parameters:
  playerIndex (byte): Index of player/unit sending message (0-3 typically)
  messageType (char): Message subtype identifier for protocol routing
  payloadData (uint*): Pointer to variable-length payload data (can be null)
  payloadSize (uint): Size of payload in bytes (0 if no payload)

Returns:
  uint*: Pointer to exception frame node containing packet, null if frame allocation fails

Special Cases:
  Server messages (playerIndex==0, messageType==0x01): Sequence counter forced to 0
  Null payload or zero payload size: Message sent with header only
  Local player (EBX==unit context): Frame node created with different offset (0x58 vs 0x4c)
  Player index 3: Frame creation entirely skipped (reserved/special handling)
  Frame allocation failure: Header and message buffers freed, null returned

Structure Layout - Message Buffer Format:
  Offset  Size  Field Name           Type      Description
  ------  ----  ---------            ----      -----------
  +0x00   2     checksumValue        ushort    CRC16 checksum of payload
  +0x02   2     payloadLength        ushort    Length of payload data in bytes
  +0x04   2     sequenceNumber       ushort    Message sequence counter for ordering
  +0x06   2     playerMode           ushort    Player mode/state flags from unit
  +0x08   1     playerIndex          byte      Sender player index (0-3)
  +0x09   1     messageType          char      Message subtype identifier
  +0x0a   1     unitFlags            byte      Unit state/mode flags
  +0x0b   1     reserved             byte      Padding for alignment
  +0x0c   n     payload              byte[n]   Variable-length payload data

0x6FC03170.name: ProcessPlayerTickMessages
0x6FC03170.comment:
Processes and queues game tick messages for all active player slots and entities.

Algorithm:
1. Retrieve current game tick count from system GetTickCount
2. Load global player list pointer (g_pUnitListHead) and validate it is non-null
3. Iterate through each player in the linked list until end:
   a. Extract next player pointer using dwClassId masking to handle linked list structure
   b. Check player mode byte at offset 0x212 to determine if player is dormant (0xFF)
   c. For dormant players, check message queue timeout (0x11C) against 50000ms threshold
   d. If timeout not exceeded and queue empty, skip to next player
   e. If timeout exceeded, call ProcessAndDestroyMessageQueues to reset queue
4. For active players, check skill timeout at offset 0x124 against 20000ms threshold
5. If skill timeout exceeded and queue is empty, rebuild network packet via BuildNetworkMessagePacket
6. Process 4 skill cooldown slots (strides at 0x168):
   a. For each skill slot, validate it points to valid skill chain
   b. Walk skill chain following offset 0x4 (next pointer)
   c. Check skill frame offset at offset 0xC+0x4 against current frame
   d. Calculate skill timing window by comparing frame offsets
   e. Check skill effect timer at offset 0x1C (0 or expired indicates send message)
   f. If expired, generate skill message with checksum and send via ProcessTickMessage
   g. Track minimum timeout across all pending skill messages
7. Process 4 entity effect slots (strides at 0x138):
   a. Skip special entity types: slot 2 (summon), slot 3 (mercenary)
   b. For valid entity slots, load game config pointer (g_pGameStateBase)
   c. Extract entity skill ID at offset 0x10 and calculate game speed adjustment
   d. Calculate entity effect timeout using formula: (skillID + gameSpeed * 1000) / speedDivisor
   e. Check effect timer at offset 0x1C (0 or expired triggers message)
   f. If expired, call ProcessUnitGameMessage with entity data at offset 0xC
   g. Track minimum timeout across all pending entity messages
8. Process 4 active effect displays (strides at 0x1DE):
   a. Load display timeout from global delay constants (g_dwEffectDisplayTimeout1Ms or g_dwEffectDisplayTimeout2Ms)
   b. Compare stored effect state at offset 0x1DE vs active state at offset 0x1E6
   c. If states differ and timer is active at offset 0x1F0, generate display update message
   d. Build message with checksums and send via ProcessTickMessage
   e. Update stored state after sending message
   f. Track minimum timeout across all pending display messages
9. Load next player from linked list and continue iteration
10. Return minimum timeout value (milliseconds until next event) or 0xFFFFFFFF if error/no players

Parameters: None

Returns:
uint - Minimum milliseconds until next scheduled message timeout event
      - Returns 0xFFFFFFFF if player list is invalid or no players are available
      - Returns 0xFFFFFFFF if InitializeGameUnit() returns null pointer

Special Cases:
- Player mode byte 0xFF identifies dormant/spectator players with different queue semantics
- Message queue timeout of 50000ms (0xC350) triggers ProcessAndDestroyMessageQueues cleanup
- Skill message timeout of 20000ms (0x4E20) triggers network packet rebuild
- Skill chain validation includes boundary checks at each node (offset 0x4)
- Skill frame offset calculation subtracts 1 from current frame for window boundary
- Entity timeout calculation incorporates game speed multiplier from offset 0x21C and divisor from 0x228
- All effect display updates are preceded by dual-layer checksum validation
- Checksum calculation uses byte-pair summation with modulo 0xFF reduction
- All timers are stored at offsets into UnitAny structure for persistence across game ticks

0x6FC035D0.name: SetActiveGameUnitContext
0x6FC035D0.comment:
Activates a new game unit context and broadcasts the change to all connected players with full synchronization.

Algorithm:
1. Acquire thread-safe critical section lock (g_CriticalSectionGameState) to prevent concurrent state modifications
2. Validate game system is initialized by checking g_pGameSystemVtable pointer is non-null (error 0x57 if null)
3. Check unit processing enabled state (g_byUnitProcessingEnabled != 0xff indicates valid state, error 0x85100070 if disabled)
4. Call InitializeGameUnit() to retrieve active unit pointer and validate it exists (error 0x120 if null)
5. Verify unit has valid data table pointer at offset +0x200 in unit structure (error 0x120 if null)
6. Load new unit index parameter from caller's stack frame [ESP+4]
7. Compare new unit index with current active unit index stored in g_dwActiveUnitIndex
8. If indices match, release lock and return 1 (no change needed, early exit)
9. Store new unit index as the current active unit in g_dwActiveUnitIndex
10. Load player list head pointer from g_pUnitListHead to begin player iteration
11. Test player count/pointer to determine if player list is empty
12. For each player node in linked list (advancing via next pointer at offset +0x4):
    a. Check player connection state at offset +0x212 (0xff = disconnected, else = connected)
    b. Skip sending message to disconnected players (0xff flag)
    c. For connected players, call BuildNetworkMessagePacket() with opcode 0x0E and 4-byte unit index payload
13. After notifying all players, call BroadcastGameStateToPlayers() to synchronize full game state across all clients
14. Test broadcast operation result in return value
15. If broadcast succeeded, release lock and return 1 (operation successful)
16. If broadcast failed or unit validation failed earlier, set error code and continue to cleanup
17. Call SetLastError() API to propagate error code to caller for error reporting
18. Release critical section lock (g_CriticalSectionGameState) to allow other threads access
19. Return 0 to caller indicating failure with error code available via GetLastError()

Parameters:
nUnitIndex: New game unit index to set as active (must reference valid initialized game unit)

Returns:
1: Unit context successfully updated and broadcasted to all connected players; operation complete
0: Unit context update failed; check GetLastError() for error code (0x57, 0x85100070, or 0x120)

Special Cases:
Error Code 0x57: Occurs when game system not initialized (g_pGameSystemVtable is null pointer)
Error Code 0x85100070: Occurs when unit processing disabled or invalid (g_byUnitProcessingEnabled == 0xff)
Error Code 0x120: Occurs when unit initialization failed or unit table invalid (pGameUnitPtr null or unitDataTable null)
Network Message Opcode 0x0E: Standard unit context update message sent to each connected player
Message Payload: 4 bytes containing the new unit index value from g_dwActiveUnitIndex
Player Disconnection Flag 0xff: Indicates player no longer connected; message sending skipped for efficiency
Early Return Value 1: Can indicate success OR early exit if unit unchanged; differentiate via GetLastError() (0 = success, else error)

Structure Layout - Player Node (accessed at g_pUnitListHead):
Offset  Size  Field Name          Type      Description
+0x0    4     pNext               pointer   Pointer to next player node in doubly-linked list
+0x4    4     pPrev               pointer   Pointer to previous player node
+0x212  1     byConnectionState   byte      Player connection flag (0xff = disconnected, other = connected)
+0x200  4     pUnitDataTable      pointer   Reference to unit data structure (must be non-null)

0x6FC036C0.name: BroadcastNetworkMessage
0x6FC036C0.comment:
Broadcasts a network message to all initialized game units with matching world coordinates.

Algorithm:
1. Validate input parameters (pMessageBuffer must be non-null, messageSize must be non-zero)
2. If validation fails, set error code 0x57 (ERROR_INVALID_PARAMETER) and return 0
3. Enter critical section (g_CriticalSectionGlobal) to ensure thread-safe access to unit list
4. Check initialization flag (g_pGameSystemVtable) to verify system is initialized
5. If not initialized, set error code 0x4b4 and return 0
6. Check sync flag (g_byUnitProcessingEnabled) - if equals 0xff, system is disabled
7. If disabled, set error 0x85100070 and return 0
8. Call InitializeGameUnit() to create new unit in game world
9. If unit creation fails (returns NULL), set error 0x85100070 and return 0
10. Load head of unit linked list from g_pUnitListHead
11. Iterate through linked list: for each unit in chain:
    a. Check validity byte at offset +0x212 (0xff = invalid/inactive)
    b. If valid, load world Y-coordinate from offset +0x1d0
    c. Compare with initialized unit's Y-coordinate at offset +0x1d0
    d. If coordinates match, broadcast message via BuildNetworkMessagePacket(2, 0x00, pMessageBuffer, messageSize)
    e. Load next unit pointer from offset +0x4 and continue iteration
12. After list iteration complete, broadcast message to newly initialized unit
13. Increment message counter (g_dwNetworkMessageCounter) using InterlockedIncrement()
14. Signal event handle (g_hSignalEventHandle) to notify any waiting threads
15. Leave critical section and return 1 (success)

Parameters:
- pMessageBuffer (uint*): Pointer to network message data buffer containing message bytes to broadcast
- messageSize (uint): Size of message buffer in bytes

Returns:
- 0: Operation failed (invalid parameters, system not initialized, sync disabled, or unit initialization failed)
- 1: Message successfully broadcasted to all matching units and initialized unit notified

Special Cases:
- Error 0x57: Invalid parameter (null buffer or zero size)
- Error 0x4b4: System not initialized (g_pGameSystemVtable is zero)
- Error 0x85100070: Either sync flag disabled (0xff) or unit initialization failed
- Unit list iteration uses linked list with 4-byte next pointer at offset +0x4
- Magic offset +0x212 (0xff indicates invalid unit, skip processing)
- Unit matching based on Y-coordinate at offset +0x1d0 (world coordinate field)
- Message counter incremented atomically to prevent race conditions
- Critical section holds lock during entire list traversal to ensure consistency

Unit Structure Layout (referenced offsets):
Offset  Size  Field Name          Type    Description
0x000   4     [next_pointer]      int*    Next unit in linked list (offset +0x4)
0x1d0   2     nWorldYCoordinate   short   Y-coordinate in world (offset +0x1d0)
0x212   1     byValidityFlag      byte    0xff = invalid/inactive unit (offset +0x212)

0x6FC037F0.name: SendNetworkBroadcastMessage
0x6FC037F0.signature: uint SendNetworkBroadcastMessage(int nUnitId, uint * pMessageData, uint dwMessageSize)
0x6FC037F0.comment:
Broadcasts a network message to all active game units with synchronization.

Algorithm:
1. Validate input parameters (nUnitId and pMessageData must be non-null/valid)
2. If parameters invalid, set last error to 0x57 (ERROR_INVALID_PARAMETER) and return 0
3. Enter critical section g_CriticalSectionGameSync to protect broadcast operation
4. Check game system initialization state from g_pGameSystemVtable
5. If system not initialized, set error 0x4b4 (ERROR_NOT_INITIALIZED) and return 0
6. Check broadcast_all flag at g_byUnitProcessingEnabled offset 0x41b4c
7. If broadcast disabled (not 0xFF), set error 0x85100070 and return 0
8. Iterate unit linked list from g_pUnitListHead with offset-based chain traversal
9. Validate each node using sentinel checks (-1 and -2 represent invalid/end states)
10. Call BuildNetworkMessagePacket (0x6fbffeb0) to prepare message for current unit
11. If packet build fails, skip to next unit without error
12. For valid units, call InitializeGameUnit (0x6fc02f40) with message and parameters
13. After list traversal, check for secondary callback via FindUnitById (0x6fc02690)
14. If callback returns valid result, invoke InitializeGameUnit with callback context
15. Increment atomic counter g_dwMessageQueueCounter at 0x6fc41a98 using InterlockedIncrement
16. Leave critical section and signal g_hSignalEventHandle via SetEvent
17. Return 1 (TRUE) on success, 0 (FALSE) on validation failure

Parameters:
  nUnitId: Unit identifier for message routing (may indicate broadcast scope)
  pMessageData: Pointer to network message buffer with serialized broadcast content
  nMessageSize: Size in bytes of the message data payload

Returns:
  1 (TRUE) if broadcast initiated successfully, 0 (FALSE) if validation fails or system uninitialized

Special Cases:
  - Parameter validation uses NEG+SBB bit-trick to detect null/invalid pointers
  - Broadcast silently succeeds even if no units match criteria
  - Orphaned units in chain are skipped without error reporting
  - Critical section ensures broadcast atomicity with respect to unit list modifications

0x6FC03940.name: BroadcastNetworkMessageToUnits
0x6FC03940.signature: int BroadcastNetworkMessageToUnits(int nUnitFilterId, uint * pMessageBuffer, uint dwMessageSize)
0x6FC03940.comment: Setting prototype: int BroadcastNetworkMessageToUnits(int nUnitFilterId, uint * pMessageBuffer, uint dwMessageSize)

0x6FC03A90.name: ShutdownGameAndCleanupResources
0x6FC03A90.comment:
Shutdown game engine and cleanup all resources before exit

Algorithm:
1. Enter critical section to synchronize with message processing threads
2. Validate game system is initialized (g_pGameSystemVtable); return 0x4b4 if not
3. Allocate and initialize game unit context via InitializeGameUnit()
4. Return 0x8 if unit allocation fails
5. Check unit for pending messages at offset +0x200; invoke vtable callback at +0x44 if found
6. First pass - iterate player linked list (g_pUnitListHead):
   - Skip players marked invalid (mode byte at offset +0x212 == 0xff)
   - For valid players: extract data at offset +0x1d0 and build network message packet
   - Process unit game messages twice per player via ProcessUnitGameMessage()
7. Second pass - iterate players and process inventory:
   - Iterate 4 inventory slots at offsets +0x138, +0x144, +0x150, +0x15c
   - Process each inventory item in linked list, calling ProcessUnitGameMessage() twice per item
8. Send final network data packet (0x65e bytes) to network layer
9. Clear global game state flags and counters
10. Process and destroy both message queues (g_pMessageQueuePtr1, g_pMessageQueuePtr2)
11. Leave critical section and call Sleep() with g_dwMessageQueueDelayMs
12. Return 1 (success)

Parameters:
- dwGameExitCode (uint): Exit code from caller (unused in function body)

Returns:
- int: 1 on successful shutdown, 0 on error conditions (game not initialized or unit allocation failure)

Special Cases:
- Error 0x4b4 (1204): Returned when game system not initialized
- Error 0x8 (8): Returned when unit context allocation fails
- Players with mode byte 0xff are inactive/removed and skipped
- Two ProcessUnitGameMessage() calls per entity ensures delivery before shutdown
- Sleep duration configured via g_dwMessageQueueDelayMs allows pending async operations
- Critical section protection prevents concurrent message processing during shutdown
- Inventory slots processed in specific order: offsets +0x138, +0x144, +0x150, +0x15c

Data Structures:
- UnitAny: Game entity with fields at offset +0x200 (pending messages), +0x212 (mode byte), +0x1d0 (data field)
- Message packet: Contains queue data at offset +0xc and +0x10 (verified in assembly)

0x6FC03CB0.name: BroadcastPlayerStateChange
0x6FC03CB0.comment:
Broadcasts a player state change to all connected clients in the game.

Algorithm:
1. Acquire critical section lock to ensure thread-safe access
2. Check if game is currently active (g_dwGameActive must be non-zero)
3. If game not active, set error 0x4B4 and return 0
4. Load the target player ID parameter (playerId)
5. Compare target player ID with current player ID (0xFF = invalid)
6. If IDs match or current player invalid, set error 0x57 and return 0
7. Find the UnitAny structure for the target player using FindUnitById
8. If unit not found, set error 0x8510006A and return 0
9. Update unit flags by ORing with 0x8 flag
10. Load unit slot value and update state fields (offset 0x210, 0x20C)
11. Iterate through all player nodes in g_pPlayerUnitListHead linked list
12. For each valid player node (not 0xFF), build network message packet
13. Use BuildNetworkMessagePacket to create state change notification
14. Release critical section lock
15. Return 1 on success

Parameters:
  playerId (byte): Target player ID for state change
  newStateValue (int): New state value to broadcast to clients

Returns:
  int: 1 if state change successfully broadcast, 0 on error

Special Cases:
  Error 0x4B4: Game not active
  Error 0x57: Invalid player ID (0xFF or mismatched with current)
  Error 0x8510006A: Unit not found for player ID

Structure Layout - UnitAny field offsets:
  Offset    Size   Field Name        Type      Description
  0x118     4      dwFlags           dword     Unit flags (ORed with 0x8)
  0x1D8     2      wSlotValue        word      Unit slot index
  0x20C     4      dwStateValue      dword     Current state value
  0x210     2      wBroadcastSlot    word      Slot to broadcast

0x6FC03E10.name: CleanupAndShutdownGame
0x6FC03E10.comment:
Synchronously shuts down and cleans up all game resources in a thread-safe manner.

Algorithm:
1. Acquire critical section lock on g_CriticalSectionGameSync for thread safety
2. Check shutdown state flag g_byCurrentPlayerId - if not 0xFF, call ShutdownGameAndCleanupResources with parameter 3
3. Release critical section lock
4. Signal and wait for all background events to complete via SignalAndWaitForEvent()
5. Re-acquire critical section lock
6. Process and clean up exception frame handlers using ProcessAndCleanupExceptionFrames()
7. Remove sentinel hash table entry with key 0x534e4554 and value 1
8. Remove sentinel hash table entry with key 0x534e4554 and value 2
9. Process all pending message queues with ProcessAllMessageQueues()
10. Clear game pause state flag g_dwGamePauseState to 0
11. Call TerminateGameResourcesOnShutdown(1) to finalize resource cleanup
12. Load and validate game handle g_hSignalEventHandle
13. If handle is non-NULL, close it with CloseHandle() and clear to NULL
14. Clear game active flag g_dwGameActive to 0
15. Clear game state flags g_dwGameStateFlags to 0
16. Release critical section lock
17. Return success code 1

Parameters:
None - operates entirely on global game state

Returns:
int - Always returns 1 to indicate successful shutdown completion

Special Cases:
- The shutdown state check (0xFF marker) prevents re-entrance and duplicate shutdown operations
- Sentinel value 0x534e4554 is a special marker for internal hash table cleanup
- Uses double critical section lock/unlock pattern to ensure atomic operations during cleanup
- All global state variables are zeroed after cleanup to prevent accidental reuse
- The game handle must be explicitly closed before zeroing to avoid resource leaks

0x6FC03EB0.name: InitializeGameState
0x6FC03EB0.signature: uint InitializeGameState(char * szPlayerName, char * szActDescription, char * szGamePassword, uint dwSeed, uint dwGameFlags, uint dwMaxPlayers, char * szInitialData, uint dwDataSize, uint dwMaxConnections, char * szConnectionInfo, char * szExtendedInfo, int * pPlayerIdOut)
0x6FC03EB0.comment:
Initialize game state with player configuration and broadcast to all connected players.

Algorithm:
1. Validate input parameters: ensure player name is not empty/null, max connections > 0, and output pointer valid
2. Set default output player ID to base offset - 1 if output pointer provided
3. Enter critical section for thread-safe game initialization
4. Check game system initialized status; abort if not ready (error 0x4B4)
5. Use default locale fallback buffer for NULL parameter pointers
6. Check if connection info buffer is empty and attempt to generate via callback at offset +0x50
7. Validate final connection info is not empty; abort if still empty (error 0x57)
8. If game already running (g_byCurrentPlayerId != -1), shutdown existing instance
9. Process all pending message queues to ensure clean state
10. Copy player name to g_szPlayerNameBuffer (max 128 bytes)
11. Copy game password to g_szGamePasswordBuffer (max 128 bytes)
12. Copy game description to g_szGameDescriptionBuffer (max 128 bytes)
13. Get current system tick count and store as game start timestamp
14. Store max players count to g_dwActiveUnitIndex
15. If game description provided, set flag bit 0 in g_dwActiveUnitIndex
16. If max connections < 2 (single/zero player), set flag bit 1 in g_dwActiveUnitIndex
17. Store game flags to g_dwPointerValueCache
18. If previous game state buffer exists, deallocate it
19. Allocate new game state buffer via arena allocator for initial game data
20. Copy initial game data to allocated buffer using DWORD-aligned loop + byte residue loop
21. Initialize first player unit (player slot 0) via InitializeGameUnit()
22. If unit creation succeeded, mark unit slot active and configure unit fields:
    - Set unit type/class at offset +0x46 to 0
    - Set player human flag at offset +0x80 to 1
    - Copy connection info to unit (128 bytes)
    - Copy extended info to unit (128 bytes)
23. Calculate player ID output as current player ID + base offset
24. Ensure array capacity for player slot storage
25. Store player slot data in global array
26. Count active player slots
27. Broadcast game state to all connected players
28. If broadcast fails, shutdown partial initialization and return error
29. Set game running flag (bit 2) in g_dwActiveUnitIndex
30. Exit critical section and return success status (1)

Parameters:
pPlayerName      - Pointer to player character name string (null-terminated, max 128 bytes)
pActDescription  - Pointer to game difficulty/act description (null-terminated, optional - defaults to empty)
pGamePassword    - Pointer to game password for access control (null-terminated, optional - defaults to empty)
dwSeed           - Random number generator seed for deterministic gameplay
dwGameFlags      - Game option flags (difficulty, expansion mode, hardcore, ladder, etc.)
dwMaxPlayers     - Maximum allowed player count for this game instance
pInitialData     - Pointer to initial game state buffer to copy (game world data)
dwDataSize       - Size of initial game state data in bytes
dwMaxConnections - Maximum simultaneous player connections allowed
pConnectionInfo  - Connection information buffer for network setup (null-terminated, optional)
pExtendedInfo    - Extended configuration data for game initialization (null-terminated, optional)
pPlayerIdOut     - Pointer to output player ID (assigned by game initialization)

Returns:
1 if game state initialized successfully and broadcast completed to all players
0 if validation failed, game system not ready, connection generation failed, or broadcast failed

Special Cases:
- NULL parameter pointers default to g_szDefaultLocaleFallback (empty fallback)
- If pConnectionInfo is NULL/empty, attempts to generate via callback function pointer at offset +0x50 within game system structure
- If game already running, shuts down previous instance with priority 2 (cleanup) before reinitializing
- Broadcast failure triggers automatic shutdown with priority 1 (minimal cleanup) and returns error code from broadcast
- Player ID output is calculated as: (g_byCurrentPlayerId + 0) + g_dwUnitBaseOffset
- Game state flags are modified by checking description and player count, setting bits 0-1 before game running flag
- Stack allocation: 0x204 bytes (516 bytes) for local buffers used by callback and memory operations
- Critical section g_CriticalSectionGlobal serializes all game initialization across multiple threads
- Calling convention: __stdcall (callee cleanup of 12 parameters = 0x30 bytes)

0x6FC04210.name: InitializeGameStateWrapper
0x6FC04210.signature: void InitializeGameStateWrapper(char * pPlayerName, char * pActDescription, char * pGamePassword, uint dwSeed, uint dwGameFlags, uint dwMaxPlayers, char * pInitialData, uint dwDataSize, uint dwMaxConnections, char * pConnectionInfo)
0x6FC04210.comment:
Parameter adaptation wrapper for InitializeGameState.

This function adapts a 10-parameter API to the internal 12-parameter InitializeGameState function
by reformatting and inserting additional parameters. It marshals all caller parameters from the
__stdcall stack frame and prepares them for the target function call with different parameter
ordering.

Algorithm:
1. Load all 10 parameters from stack at offsets relative to ESP
2. Re-marshal parameters into new stack frame for InitializeGameState
3. Insert two zero values (unused game flags and flags) after dwSeed parameter
4. Push all 12 parameters onto stack in correct order for callee
5. Call InitializeGameState with reformatted parameters
6. Return with __stdcall cleanup (RET 0x28 removes 10 DWORD parameters)

Parameters:
pPlayerName     - Player character name string (max 128 chars), passed as param 0 to callee
pActDescription - Game difficulty/act description string, passed as param 1 to callee
pGamePassword   - Access control password string, passed as param 2 to callee
dwSeed          - RNG seed for deterministic gameplay, passed as param 3 to callee
dwGameFlags     - Game configuration flags, passed as param 6 (after two 0x0 values) to callee
dwMaxPlayers    - Maximum allowed players, passed as param 5 to callee
pInitialData    - Initial game state buffer, passed as param 6 to callee
dwDataSize      - Size of initial game state in bytes, passed as param 7 to callee
dwMaxConnections- Maximum simultaneous connections, passed as param 8 to callee
pConnectionInfo - Network connection info buffer, passed as param 9 to callee

Returns:
void (return value discarded by caller)

Call Pattern:
Callee: InitializeGameState(pPlayerName, pActDescription, pGamePassword, dwSeed, 0x0, 0x0,
        pInitialData, dwDataSize, dwMaxConnections, pConnectionInfo, pExtendedInfo, pPlayerIdOut)
Calling Convention: __stdcall (callee cleans stack with RET 0x28)"

0x6FC04250.name: ProcessGameMessageQueue
0x6FC04250.comment:
Main game message queue processor - continuously fetches and processes network/system messages
Algorithm:
1. Initialize stack frame with queue handler callback pointers (12 bytes for 3 slots)
2. Loop: Fetch next message from global message queue via g_dwGameActive callback (+0x2c)
3. If no message (queue empty), exit to main game loop
4. Save all general purpose registers for duration of loop
5. Validate message payload: extract size, data pointer, and target unit ID from packet
6. Validate message integrity: size >= 0xC bytes, flags < 0x4, checksum matches computed value
7. Branch on message type flag 0x4: if set, create new unit; else find existing unit by ID
8. For unit creation: allocate unit from unit pool, initialize default state, set list pointers
9. For existing unit: search unit list by ID to locate target in active units
10. Validate message compatibility: message size, player context, location proximity to unit
11. Process unit-specific message content based on type: location, state, ability data
12. Create exception frame node, link into unit's message processing queue
13. Update unit location, timing counters, and message processing timestamps
14. Return message to queue via rejection callback for next iteration
15. Repeat message fetch loop until queue is empty
16. Return to main game loop via caller
Parameters:
(none - __stdcall, no parameters, queue accessed via global g_dwGameActive)
Returns:
void - processes all pending messages and returns control to caller
Special Cases:
Message validation failure: message rejected via g_dwGameActive callback (+0xc RejectMessage)
Unit creation: initializes with class type 0xFF/0xFF (neutral), default state 0x2
Location-based routing: searches unit lists for proximity match before location update
Unit not found: creates new unit in message-directed creation mode rather than failing
Exception frame linking: maintains per-unit message processing queues for delayed handling

0x6FC049E0.name: WaitForArrayIndexedConditions
0x6FC049E0.comment:
Waits for array-indexed condition state flags with optional millisecond timeout support.

Algorithm:
1. Clear 64-byte condition state buffer (16 dwords) at g_dwConditionIndexStateBuffer for fresh state tracking
2. Capture baseline tick count via pfnGetTickCount() for elapsed time calculation starting point
3. Initialize first iteration flag to skip sleep on initial pass through main loop
4. Enter main event processing loop that continues until conditions met or timeout:
   a. Skip sleep on first iteration; subsequent iterations sleep 10ms via pfnSleep()
   b. Process pending user events via ProcessUserEvents() to handle input
   c. Process game message queue via ProcessGameMessageQueue() to handle state updates
   d. Process player tick-based messages via ProcessPlayerTickMessages() for game logic
   e. Initialize match counter to zero and array index to zero for condition scanning
   f. If condition index array is empty (ESI == 0): immediately return 1 (success)
   g. Loop through all condition indices in array [EBX + offset*4]:
      - Load condition index value from [EBX + ECX*4]
      - Validate index is in range [0, 0x10) to prevent buffer overflow
      - Check if buffer state flag is set at g_dwConditionIndexStateBuffer[index]
      - If index valid AND state flag set: increment match counter
      - Advance to next array element
   h. After scanning all indices: test if all conditions matched (matchCount >= arrayCount)
   i. If all matched: break from loop and return 1 (success)
   j. If matches > 0 AND flagMode == 0 (return on any): return 1 (partial success)
   k. If timeout is infinite (0xFFFFFFFF): loop back to 4a
   l. If timeout is finite: get current tick count and calculate elapsed
   m. If elapsed >= timeout: return 0 (timeout exceeded, failure)
   n. Otherwise: loop back to 4a for next iteration

Parameters:
  timeoutMs: Timeout duration in milliseconds; use 0xFFFFFFFF for infinite wait

Implicit Register Parameters (__stdcall with implicit operands):
  EBX: Pointer to array of uint condition index values to monitor
  ESI: Count of elements in the condition index array
  [ESP+0x10]: Flag mode control - 0 = return on any match, nonzero = wait for all
  [ESP+0x14]: Timeout value in milliseconds (0xFFFFFFFF = infinite)

Returns:
  EAX = 1: Conditions satisfied (all matched or partial match accepted) or no conditions to wait
  EAX = 0: Timeout exceeded before condition satisfaction

Special Cases and Magic Numbers:
  Buffer size is 64 bytes (0x40) providing 16 DWORD slots (0x10)
  Valid index range is [0, 15]; indices >= 0x10 are silently skipped
  First iteration proceeds without 10ms sleep to process immediately
  Empty condition array (ESI == 0) returns success with no processing
  GetTickCount() wraps every 49.7 days; calculation handles 32-bit wrap via unsigned arithmetic
  Flag mode parameter at [ESP+0x10]: 0 = return on first match, else = require all matches
  Flag mode 0 combined with any matches (> 0) bypasses timeout check for immediate return

0x6FC04A80.name: ProcessPlayerJoinMessage
0x6FC04A80.comment:
Processes incoming player join/login message by validating credentials and initializing game state.

Algorithm:
1. Check if game database is initialized; set error if not
2. Check if player ID ordinal import is valid; set error if not
3. Acquire critical section lock to safely access player list
4. Count active player slots by iterating player linked list, checking slot marker at +0x212
5. Release critical section lock
6. Validate player count hasn't exceeded max slots limit and state flag 0x8 is not set
7. If validation fails, send error packet type 0x0a and return
8. Calculate player name string length from message[1]
9. Calculate password offset = playerNameLength + 1
10. Calculate password string length
11. Compare provided password with g_szGamePassword using case-insensitive __stricmp
12. If password mismatch, send error packet type 0x0a and return
13. Search for first available empty slot (0-254) by calling FindUnitById for each index
14. Validate slot index is not 0xff (no empty slots found)
15. Validate slot index is within g_dwMaxPlayerSlots limit
16. Initialize new game unit template via InitializeGameUnit
17. Find current player context via FindUnitByDataCompare using EBP register parameter
18. Copy player name from message+8 to playerAddress+0x8 (128 bytes)
19. Copy password from message to playerAddress+0x88 (128 bytes)
20. Load template level from piVar3+0x1d0 (ushort, 2 bytes)
21. Store template level at three player unit offsets: +0x1d8, +0x1e2, +0x1d0
22. Compare template level (+0x1d8) with current level (+0x1d0)
23. If different and unsigned difference < 0x7fff, set flag bit 0x4 at playerAddress+0x118
24. Store player slot data in persistent storage via StorePlayerSlotData
25. Reacquire critical section to recount players with new slot
26. Recount active player slots
27. If new count >= limit, set flag 0x2 at g_dwGameStateFlags
28. Release critical section
29. Broadcast updated game state to all players via BroadcastGameStateToPlayers
30. Extract game value from template level word at piVar3+0x1d0
31. Build network message type 0x08 with player count, state flags, game value, uptime seconds
32. Copy three 128-byte global data regions into stack buffer for transmission
33. Send initial game state message type 0x06 to joining player
34. Broadcast game state type 0x06 to all other active players (skip self)
35. Send lobby update message type 0x0f with 4-byte value from g_dwPointerValueCache
36. Send message type 0x09 with external data size/pointer pair
37. Send final game state broadcast type 0x06 to all other players again
38. Process pending game message linked list from player unit offset +0x180
39. For each pending message, call ProcessUnitGameMessage(pNewPlayerUnit, pMessageData)
40. Check if level change flag 0x4 is set at playerAddress+0x118
41. If flag set (level mismatch), skip event creation and return early
42. Create join event node with type=2, store player slot index at event+0xc

Parameters:
pJoinMessage: Pointer to incoming message structure containing encoded player name and password.
    Message layout: [0] unused, [1] = playerName pointer, followed by password at calculated offset

Returns:
void (no return value)

Special Cases:
- If g_dwGameInitialized == 0, sets error 0x4b4 and returns early
- If g_byCurrentPlayerId == -1, sets error 0x85100070 and returns early
- If player count >= g_dwMaxPlayerSlots or flag 0x8 set in g_dwGameStateFlags, sends error packet
- If password validation fails (__stricmp returns non-zero), sends error packet and returns
- If no empty slots found (FindUnitById returns 0 for all indices 0-255), sends error packet
- If slot index >= g_dwMaxPlayerSlots limit, sends error packet and returns
- If InitializeGameUnit returns NULL, skips event creation and returns early
- If FindUnitByDataCompare returns NULL, returns early without player initialization
- Level change flag (bit 0x4) at offset 0x118 suppresses join event creation even on success
- Critical section lock prevents race conditions during player list manipulation
- Stack frame allocates 0x1a0 bytes (416) for string buffers passed to copy functions

0x6FC04F20.name: ProcessEntityStateChangeEvents
0x6FC04F20.comment:
Processes entity state change events and broadcasts game state updates to connected players.

Algorithm:
1. Load entity list head pointer with sentinel protection (SETLE+DEC+AND trick)
2. Initialize player unit context via InitializeGameUnit()
3. Loop through linked list of entities using offset +0x4 for next pointer
4. For each entity, validate: active flag at +0x118 (bit 0x8), mode != 0xff, position delta < 0x8000
5. If all conditions met, allocate event node via CreateUserEventNode()
6. Set event type=3 and entity mode at event offsets +0x8 and +0xc
7. If network data exists at entity +0x20c, allocate buffer and copy network data
8. Clear entity active flag (+0x118), save previous mode (+0x213), mark inactive (mode=0xff at +0x212)
9. If current player valid and player context field [+0x80]==0, find minimum mode value
10. Iterate all entities to find minimum non-terminal mode (excluding connected entities)
11. If current player mode < minimum, broadcast network packet (0x0d command) with current player ID
12. Re-initialize player context and enter critical section for synchronized access
13. Count active entities by iterating list and checking mode != 0xff
14. Leave critical section and compare active count with max player slots threshold
15. If below threshold, clear state flag bit 0x2 in g_dwGameStateFlags
16. Broadcast final game state to all players via BroadcastGameStateToPlayers()
17. Move to next entity in linked list and continue processing

Parameters:
None - Function operates on global entity list and game state

Returns:
void - Function has no return value

Special Cases:
- Sentinel protection: g_pPlayerUnitListHead < 1 results in null pointer (no processing)
- Terminal mode 0xff indicates entity marked for deactivation
- Network allocation error: if AllocateMemoryFromArena fails, event node without network data
- Player validation: only occurs if g_byCurrentPlayerId != 0xff (valid player)
- Error codes: 0x4b4 for uninitialized game state, 0x85100070 for invalid player ID
- Critical section: prevents race conditions during player count validation
- Magic constants: 0x8f3 is network data block size, 0x2 is state flag bit mask

Structure Layout (Entity):
Offset  Size  Field              Type    Description
0x004   4     next_entity        ptr     Pointer to next entity in linked list
0x118   1     flags              byte    Active state flags (bit 0x8 = active)
0x200   4     connection         ptr     Network connection/player reference
0x20c   4     net_data           ptr     Network-specific data block
0x212   1     mode               byte    Entity mode (0xff = inactive/terminal)
0x213   1     prev_mode          byte    Previous mode value (saved for history)
0x1d8   2     coord_x            short   X coordinate position
0x210   2     coord_y            short   Y coordinate position

0x6FC05170.name: ProcessUnitNetworkUpdate
0x6FC05170.signature: uint ProcessUnitNetworkUpdate(uint startIndex, uint unitCount, void * * outUnitPtrs, uint * outStateInfo, uint * outUnitFlags)
0x6FC05170.comment:
Processes a batch of game units for network synchronization and state updates.

Algorithm:
1. Validate all input parameters (unitCount > 0 and all output arrays non-NULL); return 0x57 if invalid
2. Zero-initialize all three output arrays (outUnitPtrs, outStateInfo, outUnitFlags) with unitCount elements
3. Acquire critical section lock (g_CriticalSectionGlobal) for thread-safe access to unit list
4. Check game initialization state (g_dwGameInitialized); return 0x4b4 if not initialized
5. Verify current player is valid (g_byCurrentPlayerId != 0xff); return 0x85100070 if invalid
6. Call ProcessEntityStateChangeEvents to update entity state for current game state
7. Initialize new reference unit and load its unit serial number at offset +0x1d8
8. Iterate unit list and clear state change flags (0x4) for units matching the serial number
9. Release critical section lock and process exception frame list outside lock
10. Re-acquire critical section lock and verify player state again
11. Call ProcessUnitTimedEffects to handle timed effects on units
12. Get current tick count (GetTickCount) and calculate batch processing range (startIndex to startIndex + unitCount)
13. First pass: Iterate units in range and determine unit flags based on inventory state
14. For each unit, check validity flag (0x4 at offset +0x118) and inventory serial match (offset +0x180, +0xc, +0x4)
15. Store unit flags in outUnitFlags array (0x10000=base, 0x20000=inventory queue, 0x30000=both valid, 0x40000=delay)
16. Second pass: For units with 0x10000 flag and not current player, build network packets
17. Check message queue timing (g_dwMessageQueueDelayMs and g_dwMessageQueueTimeoutMs at offset +0x120)
18. Allocate packet buffer (AllocateMemoryFromArena arena 0xd) and construct network packet with unit serial and class ID
19. Validate packet checksum (ValidateBufferChecksum) and store in packet header
20. Process network tick messages (ProcessNetworkTickMessage) to transmit queued packets
21. Deallocate packet buffer after processing
22. Check unit state counter at offset +0x138; if zero/invalid, update network packet timing at offset +0x124
23. Third pass: For units passing validation, populate output arrays
24. For units with 0x20000 flag, manage inventory queue linking and node updates
25. Store inventory node pointer and size in outUnitPtrs and outStateInfo arrays
26. Increment unit serial number counter and update global mode state (g_dwUnitModeState)
27. Call InterlockedIncrement on processing counter (g_dwUnitProcessingCounter)
28. Release critical section lock and return 1 on success
29. Return 0 and set appropriate error code on any failure (0x57, 0x4b4, 0x85100070, 0x8510006b, 0x85100069)

Parameters:
  startIndex (uint): Starting index in unit array to process
  unitCount (uint): Number of units to process and size of output arrays
  outUnitPtrs (void**): Output array receiving processed unit inventory node pointers
  outStateInfo (uint*): Output array receiving inventory node data sizes
  outUnitFlags (uint*): Output array receiving unit status flags (0x10000, 0x20000, 0x30000, 0x40000)

Returns:
  1 on success with unit batch processed and network updates queued for transmission
  0 on failure with error code set via SetLastError

Special Cases:
  - All parameters must be non-NULL and unitCount > 0; returns 0x57 ERROR_INVALID_PARAMETER if violated
  - Game must be initialized (g_dwGameInitialized != 0); returns 0x4b4 if not
  - Current player must be valid (g_byCurrentPlayerId != 0xff); returns 0x85100070 if player invalid
  - Unit serial number wraps at boundary; managed by increment at offset +0x1d8
  - Units with class ID 0xff (special) skip certain network packet operations
  - Inventory timing controlled by g_dwMessageQueueTimeoutMs (timeout threshold) and g_dwMessageQueueDelayMs (delay threshold)
  - Network packet threshold: g_dwMessageQueueTimeoutMs at address 0x6fc41b40
  - Inventory validation requires serial match at offset +0xc with secondary serial at +0x4
  - Units must pass validation check (no 0x4 flag at offset +0x118) to enter output arrays
  - Message queue delay prevents excessive packet generation for units with recent queue updates

0x6FC05740.name: DequeueGameUnit
0x6FC05740.signature: int DequeueGameUnit(int * pUnitIndex, void * * ppResourceData, ushort * pResourceSize)
0x6FC05740.comment:
Dequeues the longest-idle game unit from managed resource pools.

This function safely removes a unit from the internal linked list of available units,
returning the unit's index and resource data to the caller. It uses critical sections
to ensure thread-safe access and validates all state before returning.

Algorithm:
1. Initialize output parameters to safe defaults (0 or NULL)
2. Validate that ppResourceData and pResourceSize are not NULL
3. Acquire critical section lock for thread-safe list access
4. Check if game resource system is initialized (g_dwGameInitialized)
5. Verify current player state (g_byCurrentPlayerId != -1)
6. Process any pending exception frame state changes
7. Iterate through two linked list pools sequentially:
   - First pool: g_pPlayerUnitListHead (player-created units)
   - Second pool: InitializeGameUnit pool (system units)
8. For each pool, scan all units and identify valid candidates:
   - Unit state byte at +0x212 must not be 0xFF (dead/invalid state)
   - Unit disabled flag at +0x46 bit 2 must not be set
   - Unit resource ID at +0x174 must be positive (valid)
   - Resource version at +0x4 must match unit version at +0x1d6
9. Calculate elapsed time for each valid candidate by walking resource chain:
   - Get resource pointer from unit at +0x174
   - Follow chain via +0x4 offset to find most recent timestamp
   - Calculate DVar5 (GetTickCount) - minimum timestamp = elapsed time
10. Track unit with maximum elapsed time (oldest/longest-idle)
11. If no valid unit found in either pool, return error 0x8510006b
12. Remove selected unit from linked list at +0x16c (LIST_ENTRY offset)
13. Increment unit version at +0x1d6 to invalidate cached references
14. Unlink and restore exception frame state
15. Return unit index, resource data pointer, and resource size to caller
16. Increment global dequeue counter (g_dwDequeueCounterTotal)
17. Release critical section lock

Parameters:
pUnitIndex: Pointer to receive unit index (optional, NULL allowed)
  - Output: index = unit.state_byte[+0x212] + g_dwUnitBaseOffset
ppResourceData: Pointer to receive resource data address (required)
  - Output: pointer to resource data payload (+0xc from resource base)
pResourceSize: Pointer to receive resource size in bytes (required)
  - Output: size = resource_header.size[+0x2] - 0xc

Returns:
1 (success): Unit successfully dequeued and output values set
0 (failure): Queue not initialized or no eligible unit found

Error codes written to g_dwLastErrorCode:
  0x57: Invalid parameters (ppResourceData or pResourceSize is NULL)
  0x4b4: Queue not initialized (g_dwGameInitialized == 0)
  0x85100069: Queue state corrupted after ProcessExceptionFrameList
  0x8510006b: No eligible unit found in either pool
  0x85100070: Player state invalid (g_byCurrentPlayerId == -1)

Structure References:
UnitAny at +0x0 (selected unit):
  +0x46: Flags (bit 2 = disabled flag)
  +0x174: Resource ID pointer (link to resource chain)
  +0x1d6: Unit version number (2 bytes)
  +0x212: Unit state byte (0xFF = invalid)

Resource Chain (linked at +0x174, +0x4):
  +0x4: Version number (2 bytes, matches unit version)
  +0x18: Timestamp value (dword)
  +0xc: Resource data pointer
  +0x2: Resource size (word)

Special Cases:
- Two-pool architecture: Player units scanned first, then system units
- Version tracking ensures consistency between unit and resource metadata
- Timestamp calculation walks entire resource chain to find minimum
- Critical section held for entire operation (no locks released during scanning)
- Exception frame state validated before and after processing
- Resource data pointer offset +0xc skips resource header

0x6FC059C0.name: DequeueGameUnitFromPool
0x6FC059C0.signature: int DequeueGameUnitFromPool(int * pUnitIndex, void * * ppResourceData, ushort * pResourceSize)
0x6FC059C0.comment:
Dequeues the longest-idle game unit from the managed resource pool for processing.

This function removes a game unit from the internal linked list pools, returning information
needed to access the unit's data and resource locations. It iterates through up to two linked
list pools to find the longest-idle unit, ensuring thread-safe access via critical section locks.

Algorithm:
1. Validate output parameters pUnitIndex, ppResourceData, and pResourceSize (set to 0/NULL if valid)
2. Verify ppResourceData and pResourceSize are not NULL; return error 0x57 if invalid
3. Enter critical section g_CriticalSectionGlobal to ensure thread-safe list access
4. Check if game queue is initialized (g_dwGameInitialized != 0); return error 0x4b4 if not
5. Process exception frame state changes via ProcessEntityStateChangeEvents()
6. Verify queue state is valid (g_byCurrentPlayerId != 0xFF); return error 0x85100069 if corrupted
7. Get current tick count via GetTickCount() for time-based idle calculation
8. Initialize poolIterationIndex = 0, pBestUnitFound = NULL, maxElapsedTicks = 0
9. Loop through two pools (pool 0 = g_pPlayerUnitListHead, pool 1 = InitializeGameUnit result):
   a. For each unit in current pool, check if valid (state byte at offset +0x212 != 0xFF)
   b. Load resource pool ID at offset +0x18c; skip if <= 0
   c. Walk resource chain at offset +0xc (linked list of resources)
   d. Track resource timestamp at offset +0x18 for each resource
   e. Calculate elapsed time = current_tick - resource_timestamp
   f. If elapsed time > maxElapsedTicks, update maxElapsedTicks and pBestUnitFound
10. Increment poolIterationIndex; if <= 1, continue to next pool
11. Verify a unit was found (pBestUnitFound != NULL); return error 0x8510006b if none found
12. Load resource list at pBestUnitFound + 0x18c (conditional mask handles invalid values)
13. Remove unit from linked list at offset +0x184 (24-byte double-linked list header)
14. Increment unit version counter at offset +0x1da (word size)
15. Restore exception frame state via UnlinkAndRestoreExceptionFrameIndexed()
16. Set output pUnitIndex = (unit_state_byte at offset +0x212) + g_dwUnitBaseOffset (if not NULL)
17. Set output ppResourceData = (resource_base_pointer + 0xc offset)
18. Set output pResourceSize = (resource_size_word at offset +0x2) - 0xc
19. Increment global dequeue counter g_dwDequeueCounterTotal
20. Leave critical section and return 1 for success

Parameters:
pUnitIndex: Pointer to receive unit index value (optional), derived from state byte at unit offset
+0x212, then added to g_dwUnitBaseOffset. Set to NULL to skip output.
ppResourceData: Pointer to receive resource data buffer pointer (required), calculated as resource
base pointer + 0xc offset bytes
pResourceSize: Pointer to receive resource size in bytes (required), calculated as word value at
resource offset +0x2 minus 0xc bytes

Returns:
1 (0x1) if unit successfully dequeued and all output parameters populated with valid data
0 (0x0) if operation failed for any reason (see error codes written to g_dwLastErrorCode)

Error Codes:
0x57: Parameter validation failed - ppResourceData or pResourceSize is NULL
0x4b4: Queue not initialized - g_dwGameInitialized is zero
0x85100070: Invalid initialization state detected
0x85100069: Queue state corrupted after processing exception frames
0x8510006b: No eligible units found after scanning both resource pools

Thread Safety:
Entire operation protected by critical section lock (g_CriticalSectionGlobal). Function acquires
lock at start and releases before returning. All global state access is synchronized.

Special Cases:
- Handles two separate linked-list pools in sequence for load distribution
- Resource chains may contain multiple linked resources; traverses full chain for each unit
- Version tracking at unit offset +0x1da maintains consistency between unit and resource metadata
- Uses tick-count-based aging to select longest-idle unit
- Conditional masking at offset +0x18c prevents invalid resource pool IDs from being dereferenced
- Manages exception frame restoration for cleanup guarantees

0x6FC05C10.name: InitializePlayerGameConnection
0x6FC05C10.signature: int InitializePlayerGameConnection(uint dwGameInitFlags, byte * pOptionalMessageBuffer, uint * pOptionalDataBuffer, uint * pPlayerData, uint * pGameStateData, int * pPlayerSlotIndex)
0x6FC05C10.comment:
Initializes a player's game connection and prepares the player unit for multiplayer gameplay.

Algorithm:
1. Validate player count parameter and check game initialization state
2. Enter critical section to ensure thread-safe game state access
3. Validate game state is active; if not, return error code 0x4b4
4. Provide default buffer handlers if NULL pointers are passed by caller
5. Invoke custom buffer handler to populate message/data buffers if callback exists
6. Call protocol handler with populated buffers to initialize network connection
7. Verify game state checksums match before/after protocol initialization
8. Find player unit matching the current slot ID
9. Initialize player unit flags (bits at +0x204, +0x1d4, +0x1de, +0x1cc)
10. Build network message packets for game synchronization (types 1, 2)
11. Wait for synchronization events with timeout (handles 0x2 and 0x9/0xa)
12. Parse slot data from sync response and apply to player unit
13. Store player slot information and leave critical section
14. Return success (0x1) if all stages complete, or error code on failure

Parameters:
- gameInitFlags: uint containing game initialization options and flags
- pOptionalMessageBuffer: byte* to optional message buffer (can be NULL, uses default if so)
- pOptionalDataBuffer: uint* to optional data buffer (can be NULL, uses default if so)
- pPlayerData: uint* to player-specific data buffer for connection initialization
- pGameStateData: uint* to game state data buffer containing game context
- pPlayerSlotIndex: int* pointer to write calculated player slot index on success

Returns:
- 0x1 (success) if player initialization completes successfully
- 0x0 (failure) if critical section entry fails or protocol handler fails
- 0x4b4 if game state is not initialized/active
- 0x8 if player unit matching slot cannot be found
- 0x57 if game state buffer is invalid/null
- 0x85100067 if synchronization timeout occurs during initial sync
- 0x4d0 if synchronization timeout occurs during final sync
- 0x85100069 if player slot assignment fails (slot marked as 0xff)
- 0x85100079 if game state checksums don't match before/after protocol call

Special Cases:
- If NULL buffers provided, function allocates default 0x80-byte buffers on stack
- Player slot ID (0xff = invalid) is read from global g_byCurrentPlayerId
- Game state base offset stored in g_dwUnitBaseOffset
- Critical section protected by g_CriticalSectionGameSync (0x6fc45a24)
- Maximum player count from g_dwUnitBaseOffset (after decrement operation)
- Shutdown flag (0x6fc41b4c) determines game behavior on sync timeout
- Each player unit contains 0x88-byte state block starting at offset +0x8

0x6FC06030.name: ProcessAndCountGameUnits
0x6FC06030.comment:
Process and count active game units with timed effects
Validates that pUnitCountOut pointer is not NULL, enters a critical section
to safely access game state, and iterates through all active game units.
For each unit with active timed effects, counts the number of items in its
inventory and returns the total count via the output parameter.

Algorithm:
1. Check if pUnitCountOut pointer is NULL - return 0 if invalid
2. Enter critical section lock (g_pEnterCriticalSection at 0x6fc33254)
3. Load game state from g_dwGameInitialized (0x6fc45834)
4. Zero the output count parameter [EDI + 0x0]
5. If game is not initialized, set error code 0x4b4 and exit
6. Load first unit from game state and validate it exists
7. Check unit state byte at offset +0x200 (unit mode/state flags)
8. If unit state is 0, search for first active unit in g_pPlayerUnitListHead
9. Iterate through unit linked list (next pointer at offset +0x4)
10. For each unit with non-zero state at offset +0x200:
    a. Call ProcessUnitTimedEffects to update unit timers
    b. Load item list pointer from unit at offset +0x180
    c. Count items by traversing linked list (next pointer at offset +0x4)
    d. Increment output counter for each item found
11. Leave critical section lock (g_pLeaveCriticalSection at 0x6fc33258)
12. Return 1 (success) in EAX, 0 if error detected

Parameters:
- pUnitCountOut: Pointer to DWORD where total item count will be stored.
  Receives sum of all items in all active units' inventories.

Returns:
- 1 (success): Valid unit count computed and stored in *pUnitCountOut
- 0 (failure): NULL pointer provided or game not initialized

Special Cases:
- NULL pointer check uses NEG/SBB technique to detect NULL without conditional
- Error codes stored at 0x6fc45388 (g_dwLastErrorCode) before return
- Critical section prevents race conditions during unit list traversal
- Unit state transitions cause search to find next active unit
- Offset +0x200 represents unit state/mode field (typically 4-byte aligned)
- Offset +0x180 represents unit's item list head pointer
- Offset +0x4 represents next pointer in linked lists

0x6FC06150.name: MainGameLoop
0x6FC06150.comment:
Main game loop that coordinates game processing with synchronization.

Algorithm:
1. Load shutdown flag (g_dwSignalInProgress) for early exit check
2. Initialize nextTickTimeout to INFINITE (0xffffffff)
3. Load critical section and WaitForSingleObject function pointers into registers
4. Main synchronization loop:
   a. Call WaitForSingleObject with current timeout to wait for sync event
   b. Convert result: (result == 0) becomes 1 for signaled, else -1 for timeout
   c. Check g_dwSignalInProgress for shutdown signal, exit if set
   d. Enter critical section to protect shared game state
   e. Check g_dwGameInitialized, skip processing if already shutdown
   f. If event was signaled (result == 0), process pending events:
      - ProcessUserEvents() - handle user input/events
      - ProcessGameMessageQueue() - process accumulated game messages
   g. Call ProcessPlayerTickMessages() to get next wake-up timeout value
   h. Leave critical section
   i. Check g_dwSignalInProgress again, loop if not shutdown, else exit
5. Return 0 (always succeeds)

Parameters:
  (none) - Function uses global synchronization state and critical section

Returns:
  void - Always returns successfully after shutdown signal

Special Cases:
  - INFINITE timeout (0xffffffff) used for indefinite wait on first iteration
  - Critical section protects against race conditions when shutdown occurs
  - Shutdown flag checked both before and after critical section entry
  - If shutdown occurs during WaitForSingleObject, event processing is bypassed
  - Event result conversion (NEG/SBB/INC) produces 1 for signaled, -1 for timeout
  - Double-checked shutdown: before critical section and after leaving it

Global State:
  - g_dwSignalInProgress: Shutdown signal flag
  - g_hSignalEventHandle: Win32 event handle for synchronization
  - g_CriticalSectionGlobal: CRITICAL_SECTION for thread-safe state access
  - g_dwGameInitialized: Game state validity flag

0x6FC061E0.name: InitializeGameThread
0x6FC061E0.comment:
Initializes the game's main worker thread and synchronization event handle on first call.

Algorithm:
1. Load main game event handle from g_hSignalEventHandle
2. If event not yet created, call CreateEventA() with default parameters
3. Store created event handle in g_hSignalEventHandle for later use
4. Load main game thread handle from g_hMainGameThreadHandle
5. If thread not yet created, prepare thread creation parameters
6. Initialize game loop state flag g_dwGameLoopState to 0
7. Call CreateThread() to launch MainGameLoop function
8. Store created thread handle in g_hMainGameThreadHandle
9. Set thread priority to THREAD_PRIORITY_NORMAL (2) via SetThreadPriority()
10. If caller provided output pointer in ESI, write event handle to *ESI
11. Verify both event and thread handles are non-NULL
12. Return 1 if both handles created successfully, 0 if any handle creation failed

Parameters:
ESI (IMPLICIT): Pointer to HANDLE output buffer for storing event handle (may be NULL to skip output)

Returns:
EAX: 1 (TRUE) if both event and thread initialized successfully, 0 (FALSE) if any initialization failed

Special Cases:
- Idempotent: Multiple calls are safe, only creates handles on first invocation
- Implicit ESI parameter: Caller must provide valid HANDLE* in ESI or set to NULL to skip output
- Synchronous creation: Thread is created immediately and may begin executing before function returns
- Manual-reset event: Allows multiple threads to wait simultaneously until explicitly reset
- THREAD_PRIORITY_NORMAL used for game loop to prevent starvation of other OS threads

0x6FC06260.name: ApplyPatchesFromRegistry
0x6FC06260.comment:
Applies patches from registry-stored patch list by parsing and executing patch commands

Algorithm:
1. Validate input parameter is not NULL, return error 0x57 if invalid
2. Enter critical section to protect global patch data structures
3. Query registry value "Patches" containing null-terminated patch file paths
4. Get current module filename and find last directory separator character
5. Iterate through each patch file path in the registry patch list
6. Load patch file with OpenFileArchive to parse MPQ/patch format
7. Call VerifyArchiveSignature to validate patch signature using cryptographic hash
8. Verify patch status (must be >= 5) indicating successful validation
9. Extract "Prepatch.lst" manifest from patch file to validate structure
10. Allocate buffer and read patch data from file handle
11. Parse patch command list, iterating line-by-line through commands
12. For delete command: call DeleteFileA to remove target file from patch directory
13. For extract command: open target file in patch, allocate buffer, decompress with ReadDataToBuffer
14. Write extracted data to output file using CreateFileA and WriteFile
15. For execute command: append program path to null-terminated command list
16. Build complete command line in memory with multiple commands separated by null bytes
17. Create new processes for each command using CreateProcessA with CREATE_NEW_CONSOLE (0x20)
18. Close process and thread handles after creation
19. Release all file handles and memory allocations (DeallocateMemoryBlock)
20. Return success (1) with *pStatusCode=0x2, or failure (0) with *pStatusCode=0xFFFFFFFF

Parameters:
  pStatusCode: Pointer to uint32 for result status codes
    Returns 0x2 on success, 0xFFFFFFFF on I/O error, 0x57 on invalid parameter, 0x0 if no patches found

Returns:
  1 - Successfully applied all patches and created processes
  0 - Failed to read registry or create processes

Special Cases:
  - If registry "Patches" value is empty, returns 0 with *pStatusCode=0x0
  - Patch files with signature status < 5 return 0 with *pStatusCode=0xFFFFFFFF
  - Command line buffer maximum is 1024 bytes; multiple processes created if needed
  - All file operations protected by critical section g_CriticalSectionPatchGlobal
  - Process creation uses CREATE_NEW_CONSOLE flag (0x20) for visible update window
  - Module path truncation at last backslash separates directory from filename

0x6FC068B0.name: LoadCapsDataFromArchive
0x6FC068B0.comment:
Loads capability data (caps.dat) from a game archive file.

Algorithm:
1. Allocate local variables for archive handle, file handle, and buffer pointer (all NULL-initialized)
2. Call OpenFileArchive to open the archive file and obtain archive handle
3. Return NULL if archive open fails (step exit)
4. Call VerifyArchiveSignature to validate archive structure
5. Check signature validation: proceed if no error OR if error pointer is NULL OR >= 0x4
6. Call OpenAndValidateGameFile to locate and open caps.dat within archive
7. Acquire critical section lock (g_CriticalSectionGameSync) for thread-safe access
8. Check file descriptor at offset 0x43: if -1, file is virtual (size at [pFileHandle[0x45] + 8])
9. If file descriptor != -1, call GetFileSize API to get physical file size
10. Call AllocateMemoryFromArena to allocate buffer (size determined in step 8 or 9)
11. Call ReadDataToBuffer to read file contents into allocated buffer
12. Release file handle via ReleaseFileHandleWithRefCount if handle is non-NULL
13. Release archive handle via ReleaseGameObjectReference if handle is non-NULL
14. Return pointer to allocated buffer containing caps.dat contents

Parameters:
  pArchivePath (uint*) - Path to archive file (passed via ECX register per __fastcall convention)

Returns:
  Pointer to uint array containing loaded caps.dat file contents
  NULL if any operation fails (archive open, validation, or file operations)

Special Cases:
  File descriptor virtual flag: Offset 0x43 value of -1 indicates file is virtual with size stored at memory location [pFileHandle[0x45] + 8]
  File descriptor physical flag: Offset 0x43 value != -1 indicates standard file handle requiring GetFileSize() call
  Critical section: Synchronizes file size determination with other threads accessing same file handle
  Resource cleanup: All handles released regardless of intermediate failure to prevent resource leaks

0x6FC069A0.name: LoadAndInitializeProviderLibraries
0x6FC069A0.comment:
Loads and initializes all provider libraries from the provider directory.

Algorithm:
1. Check initialization flag (g_dwProviderInitializationFlag) to ensure one-time execution
2. If already initialized, return immediately; else mark as initialized
3. Get module filename via GetModuleFileNameA() into szModulePath buffer
4. Extract directory path by scanning backward for final backslash character
5. Build search pattern by appending "*.snp" to directory path
6. Find first .snp file using FindFirstFileA(), get search handle
7. For each provider file found:
   a. Build full provider DLL path using wsprintfA with path + filename
   b. Load provider data archive via LoadCapsDataFromArchive()
   c. Check archive loaded successfully, if not deallocate and skip
   d. Load provider DLL using LoadLibraryA()
   e. Check DLL loaded successfully, if not deallocate archive and skip
   f. Get SnpQuery export function via GetProcAddress()
   g. Check export exists, if not deallocate and skip
   h. Call SnpQuery(0, ...) to query first provider entry
   i. Loop through all provider entries from SnpQuery:
      - Validate provider data size >= 0x24 (minimum structure size)
      - Check flag 0x10000000 is NOT set (invalid provider marker)
      - Extract provider strings and copy to allocated node:
        * Copy provider DLL path to node offset +0x82 (260 bytes max)
        * Copy provider index to node offset +0x10c
        * Copy provider type to node offset +0x110
        * Copy provider name (max 128 bytes) to node offset +0x114
        * Copy second name (max 128 bytes) to node offset +0x194
        * Copy type info array (9 DWORDs) to node offset +0x214
        * Decrement final type info entry by 0x10
      - Find sorted insertion point using CompareProvidersByTypeAndContent()
      - Insert provider node into linked list sorted by type/content
      - Increment provider counter
      - Call SnpQuery with incremented index for next entry
   j. Loop until SnpQuery returns 0 (no more entries)
8. Find next provider file using FindNextFileA()
9. Repeat for all .snp files
10. Close file search handle via FindClose()
11. Free all provider DLLs via FreeLibrary()
12. Free archive data via DeallocateMemoryBlock()

Parameters:
None - function uses global state:
  g_dwProviderInitializationFlag: Tracks initialization state (set to 1 on first call)
  g_hModuleInstance: Module handle for GetModuleFileNameA()
  g_pMemoryPoolHead: Memory pool for allocating provider nodes
  g_pProviderListHead: Head of linked list for storing providers
  g_pSortedProviderList: Sorted list pointer for tree operations

Returns:
void - modifies global provider linked list (g_pProviderListHead)

Special Cases:
- Sets error code 0x57 (ERROR_INVALID_PARAMETER) when module path extraction fails
- Silently skips .snp files where archive load fails
- Silently skips providers without valid SnpQuery export
- Silently skips provider entries with data size < 0x24
- Silently skips provider entries with invalid flag bit 0x10000000 set
- Provider type info final entry (offset +0x21c) has 0x10 subtracted (reserved field)
- Uses linked list doubly-linked structure with forward/backward pointers
- Creates sorted insertion through callback comparison function

0x6FC06D90.name: EnumeratePropertiesWithCallback
0x6FC06D90.comment:
Enumerate all properties in the system and invoke a callback for each valid property.

ALGORITHM:
1. Load callback function pointer and property list base from stack parameters
2. Validate pPropertyListBase: must be non-null and not equal to 0x24 (invalid marker)
3. Validate pCallbackFunction: must be non-null (use NEG + SBB + AND pattern to check both)
4. If validation fails, set error code 0x57 (ERROR_INVALID_PARAMETER) via SetLastError and return 0
5. Enter critical section at g_CriticalSectionGlobal for thread-safe enumeration
6. Call LoadAndInitializeProviderLibraries() to ensure property system is initialized
7. Load property list head address from global g_pSortedProviderList into loop register
8. Test property count; if count <= 0, skip loop and go to cleanup
9. For each property node in linked list:
   a. Load property ID from node offset +0x110
   b. Test property ID non-zero; if zero, skip to next iteration
   c. Load property name pointer from node offset +0x114 into EDI
   d. Test name pointer non-null; if null, skip to next iteration
   e. Test first byte of name string not null terminator; if empty, skip to next iteration
   f. Load constraint data pointer from node offset +0x214 into ECX
   g. Call ValidatePropertyConstraints() with constraint data pointer
   h. Test constraint validation result; if invalid (0), skip callback invocation
   i. Load property data pointer from node offset +0x194
   j. Push property data pointer, name pointer, property ID, callback extra param onto stack
   k. Call user-provided callback function with (nPropertyId, szPropertyName, pPropertyData, nExtraParam)
   l. Test callback return value; if zero, terminate enumeration (set node pointer to 0)
   m. Reload property count from g_pSortedProviderList for loop continuation check
10. Check loop continuation conditions:
    a. Test g_dwProviderInitializationFlag (continuation flag); if zero, exit loop
    b. Test property count >= 1; if not, exit loop
    c. Test current node pointer non-zero; if zero, exit loop
11. Load next node pointer from current node offset +0x4
12. Verify next node pointer valid; if valid, jump back to step 9a; otherwise exit loop
13. Pop preserved registers (EDI, EBX, ESI) to restore caller's state
14. Leave critical section via LeaveCriticalSection()
15. Set return value to 1 (success)
16. Restore EBP and return to caller with RET 0x8 (clean up 2 parameters)

PARAMETERS:
- pPropertyListBase (void *): Pointer to property list structure; must be non-null and not equal to 0x24 (invalid marker); used to retrieve property list head from global g_pSortedProviderList
- pCallbackFunction (void *): Function pointer to user-provided callback invoked for each valid property; callback receives (int nPropertyId, char *szPropertyName, void *pPropertyData, int nExtraParam) and returns int (0 to terminate, non-zero to continue)

RETURNS:
- 1: Enumeration completed successfully; all valid properties processed or callback terminated with return value 0
- 0: Invalid parameters (pPropertyListBase null, pPropertyListBase == 0x24, or pCallbackFunction null); error code 0x57 (ERROR_INVALID_PARAMETER) set via SetLastError()

SPECIAL CASES:
- Magic value 0x24 in pPropertyListBase is treated as invalid even if pointer is technically non-null
- Empty property name (first byte null terminator) causes property to be skipped
- Null property ID causes property to be skipped
- Callback can terminate enumeration early by returning 0; subsequent properties not processed
- Global g_dwProviderInitializationFlag acts as external continuation flag; if zero, enumeration terminates
- Property list traversal stops if any required pointer (name, constraint data, property data) is null

STRUCTURE LAYOUT:
Property Node Structure (offsets verified from assembly instructions):
Offset  Size  Field Name      Type      Description
+0x4    4     nextNode        void*     Link to next property node in linked list (offset +0x4)
+0x110  4     propertyId      int       Unique property identifier (non-zero indicates valid)
+0x114  4     propertyName    char*     Pointer to null-terminated property name string
+0x194  ...   propertyData    void*     Property-specific data block passed to callback
+0x214  ...   constraintData  void*     Constraint/validation structure validated before callback

0x6FC06E70.name: InitializeNetworkProvider
0x6FC06E70.signature: int InitializeNetworkProvider(int nProviderType, int nPoolSize1, int nPoolSize2, int nPoolSize3, int nPoolSize4)
0x6FC06E70.comment:
Initializes and configures a Storm Network Protocol (SNP) provider for network communication.

Algorithm:
1. Clean up any existing provider resources to reset state
2. Call provider library initialization routine to set up provider list
3. Load provider list pointer from g_pNetworkProviderList
4. Validate provider count; if invalid, set to 0 and jump to error
