0x6FC2D852.comment:
Converts double-precision floating-point to string representation in buffer.

Algorithm:
1. Load global stack guard seed and XOR with current EBP frame pointer
2. Save computed security cookie to stack for overflow detection
3. Load input double value from pointer parameter and interpret as STRFLT

9. Call __cftof2 to append null terminator character to complete string
10. Verify security cookie XOR with EBP matches saved value to detect overflow

bufferSize (size_t): Maximum capacity in characters available in output buffer

Stack overflow: Cookie verification via VerifyStackCanary on mismatch
Buffer structure: STRFLT interpretation of double provides sign and exponent

0x6FC2DA24.name: GetProcessorCountForHyperThreading
0x6FC2DA24.comment:
Retrieves the logical processor count for systems with Hyper-Threading support

Algorithm:
1. Initialize SEH (Structured Exception Handling) frame with size 0xc bytes
2. Push exception frame size (0xc) onto stack
3. Push exception handler function address (0x6fc37bb8) onto stack
4. Call SEH prolog to set up exception handling frame (__SEH_prolog)
5. Clear processorCount local variable at [EBP-0x1c] to 0
6. Clear exception handler flag at [EBP-0x4] to 0
7. Preserve XMM0 register state (MOVAPD XMM0,XMM1) for floating-point operations
8. Set default processorCount = 1 at [EBP-0x1c] (assumes single processor by default)
9. Jump unconditionally to cleanup_and_exit label (no CPUID executed in this version)
10. Set exception handler flag = -1 (0xffffffff) at [EBP-0x4] for cleanup activation
11. Load processorCount from [EBP-0x1c] into EAX for return value
12. Call SEH epilog to clean up exception frame and restore original stack (__SEH_epilog)
13. Return processorCount value in EAX register

Parameters:
None - function takes no parameters

Returns:
int - Logical processor count, defaults to 1. Returns 1 if CPUID execution fails or is not available.

Special Cases:
- Function uses Structured Exception Handling (SEH) to safely execute potentially unsafe CPUID instruction
- Default return value is 1 (single processor fallback)
- Only called from DetectCPUCapabilities when CPU reports Hyper-Threading capability (CPUID.1 ECX bit 28 set)
- XMM0 register is explicitly preserved during execution to maintain SSE state
- Exception frame size is 0xc bytes (3 DWORD stack locations)
- Function is part of CPU capability detection sequence for Hyper-Threading detection

0x6FC2DA59.name: DetectCPUCapabilities
0x6FC2DA59.comment:
Detects CPU capabilities using CPUID instruction and EFLAGS modifications. Determines if CPU supports CPUID instruction by testing the modifiability of the ID flag (bit 21) in the EFLAGS register. If CPUID is supported, executes CPUID functions 0 and 1 to extract brand string, version information, and feature bits. Specifically checks for Hyper-Threading support (bit 28 of CPUID.1 ECX), and if present, determines the number of logical processors. Also detects AMD processors by comparing the CPUID brand string against "AuthenticAMD". Sets global flags indicating Hyper-Threading capability and AMD processor detection. Includes stack canary verification for buffer overflow protection.

Algorithm:
1. Load stack canary XOR seed from g_dwStackGuardSeed and XOR with stack frame address
2. Test EFLAGS ID bit (0x200000) modifiability by toggling and reading back
3. If ID bit not modifiable, CPUID not supported - skip CPU detection at cpuid_not_supported label
4. Execute CPUID function 0 (leaf 0) to get max function and brand string parts
5. Execute CPUID function 1 (leaf 1) to get version info (EAX) and feature bits (ECX)
6. Initialize both global flags to 0
7. Check bit 28 of CPUID.1 ECX feature bits for Hyper-Threading capability
8. If Hyper-Threading capable, call GetProcessorCountForHyperThreading to get processor count
9. If processor count > 0, set g_dwHTCapableFlag to 1
10. Compare brand string with "AuthenticAMD" (12 bytes)
11. Extract family from bits [11:8] and model from bits [7:4] of CPUID.1 EAX
12. Extract extended family from bits [27:20] and extended model from bits [19:16]
13. Calculate actual family and model using conditional logic for extended values
14. If string comparison failed or core count invalid, set g_dwAMDProcessorFlag to 1
15. Verify stack canary by XORing with current stack frame before return

Parameters:
None - function takes no parameters

Returns:
void - Updates two global CPU detection flags:
  g_dwHTCapableFlag (0x6fc46900): Set to 1 if Hyper-Threading capable and processor count > 0
  g_dwAMDProcessorFlag (0x6fc468fc): Set to 1 if AMD processor detected

0x6FC2DB30.name: PrepareAndComputeFPUPower
0x6FC2DB30.comment:
Prepares x87 FPU stack values and dispatches to power computation kernel.

Algorithm:
1. Save current EBP (frame pointer) via PUSH
2. Establish new stack frame with MOV EBP, ESP
3. Allocate 16 bytes of local stack space for FPU double precision values
4. Align ESP to 16-byte boundary (required for SSE/FPU alignment)
5. Exchange FPU stack top two values: ST0 ↔ ST1 (swap exponent and base)
6. Store ST1 (base value after swap) to [ESP+0x8] as double precision
7. Store ST0 (exponent value after swap) to [ESP+0x0] as double precision
8. Call ComputeBaseToExponentPower with prepared arguments
9. Restore stack frame and return to caller

Parameters:
- ST0 (FPU implicit): Exponent value in extended precision (float10)
- ST1 (FPU implicit): Base value in extended precision (float10)

Returns:
- void: Result handled by ComputeBaseToExponentPower and returned via FPU

Special Cases:
- Caller (ComputePowerWithCPUCheck) verifies CPU capability flags before calling
- MXCSR and FPU control word are validated by caller to ensure proper mode
- 16-byte stack alignment required for compatibility with underlying computation
- Only called when SSE and FPU conditions are verified by caller

0x6FC2DB49.name: ComputeBaseToExponentPower
0x6FC2DB49.signature: int ComputeBaseToExponentPower(int pResultStorage, double dBase, int iExponentInteger, int uiExponentHigh)
0x6FC2DB49.comment:
Computes base^exponent using IEEE 754 double precision with table-driven mantissa approximation.

Algorithm:
1. Extract IEEE 754 exponent and mantissa components via bit shifting (right shift by 44 bits for exponent extraction)
2. Perform initial table lookup using mantissa normalization index from g_dMantissaTableBase (offset by uintTableIndex*4)
3. Validate exponent range [0x10, 0x7fef); jump to special case handling if outside normal range
4. For normal case: enter main mantissa processing loop executing iterative table-driven polynomial approximation
5. Extract secondary exponent field via right shift by 38 bits and lookup scaling coefficients from g_dSecondaryMantissaTable
6. Perform second-level table lookup with refined index via g_dTertiaryScalingTable and accumulate polynomial terms
7. Refine mantissa using polynomial coefficients (g_dPolynomialCoeff1 through g_dPolynomialCoeff5) with iterative multiplication
8. Accumulate scaled exponent contribution from lookup tables (g_dExponentAdjustmentTable, g_dExponentRefinementTable)
9. Compute final result using accumulated mantissa and exponent with 128.0 scaling factor (0x4060)
10. Validate result mantissa via bounds check against 0x1ff7f (upper) and -0x1e1ff (lower) with underflow/overflow detection
11. Apply underflow (result < min double) or overflow (result > max double) handling returning normalized values
12. Dispatch to DispatchMathematicalOperation with operation code in EDX for final IEEE rounding and special case handling

Parameters:
- pResultStorage (int): Pointer to 80-bit extended precision storage for return value (x87 FPU format)
- dBase (double): Base value in IEEE 754 double precision format; supports all floating-point classes
- iExponentInteger (int): Integer component from parameter packing (unused in standard case, for edge case handling)
- uiExponentHigh (uint): High-order 32 bits of exponent from parameter packing

Returns:
- float10 via x87 FPU: 80-bit extended precision result stored in x87 register ST0
- Return values: normal finite results, infinity (base > 1 with large exponent), zero (base < 1 with large exponent)
- Special cases: 0^0 = 1, 0^negative = infinity, 1^any = 1, negative_base^integer handled per sign

Special Cases:
- Zero base with positive exponent: returns 0.0 (operation code 0x1a)
- Zero base with negative/zero exponent: returns infinity (operation code 0x1d)
- Base 1.0 with any exponent: returns 1.0 (special mantissa detection at offset 0x3ff00000)
- Base -1.0 with even integer exponent: returns 1.0; with odd exponent: returns -1.0
- Subnormal base values: normalized via scaling by 2^64 before main algorithm, restart loop
- Subnormal exponent (exponent range [0x10, 0x7fef)): bounds validation at 0x6fc2dbb0-dbb6
- NaN base: dispatched with operation code 0x3ee for IEEE special value handling
- Infinity base: dispatched with operation codes 0x18-0x1d based on sign/exponent configuration
- Overflow condition: result exponent exceeds 0x40a0, dispatch operation code 0x18 (infinity result)
- Underflow condition: result exponent below 0x3c70, dispatch operation code 0x19 (zero/subnormal result)
- Mantissa index bounds validation: index range [0x1ff7f, -0x1e1ff] at offset 0x6fc2dd83-dd99

Structure Layout (IEEE 754 Double Precision):
Offset    Size    Field Name              Type       Description
0x00      8       Double Value            double     Full 64-bit IEEE 754 value
0x00      1       Mantissa Bits [0:7]     byte       Low 8 bits of normalized mantissa
0x04      4       Exponent+Sign [0:31]    uint       Bits [32:63]: exponent (11 bits) + sign (1 bit)
0x06      2       Exponent Field [0:15]   ushort     Bits [52:62]: biased exponent (11 bits)
0x07      1       Sign Bit                byte       Bit 63: sign (1=negative, 0=positive)

0x6FC2E7DE.name: ComputeExtendedPrecisionExponent
0x6FC2E7DE.signature: float10 ComputeExtendedPrecisionExponent(float10 * __return_storage_ptr__, float10 ldInputValue, byte bFlags)
0x6FC2E7DE.comment:
Computes extended-precision floating-point exponent approximation using F2XM1 (2^x - 1).

Algorithm:
1. Load input value from FPU stack (ST0) and compute absolute value
2. Compare absolute value against global threshold constant (g_f10ExponentThreshold)
3. Store comparison flags in FPU status word at [EBP - 0xa0]
4. Test condition flags at [EBP - 0x9f] for bit pattern 0x41
5. If flags are set: perform early exit with status
6. If flags clear: proceed with fractional calculation:
   a. Round input value to nearest integer using FRNDINT
   b. Calculate fractional part: original_value - rounded_value
   c. Test fractional part against zero
7. Take absolute value of fractional part
8. Compute 2^x - 1 approximation using F2XM1 instruction
9. Return result in FPU stack (ST0) with status flags in DL

Parameters:
- inputValue: Extended-precision floating-point input (10 bytes, accessed via FPU stack ST0)
- flags: Control flags affecting computation path (undefined1 type, 1 byte)

Returns:
- Extended-precision result of 2^(fractional_part) - 1 in FPU stack ST0
- Status flags in DL register indicating comparison and test results

Special Cases:
- Uses global threshold constant at g_f10ExponentThreshold (0x6fc41e5e)
- F2XM1 requires absolute value of input; instruction domain: -1 < x <= 1
- Two computation paths: early exit for certain flag patterns, full fractional calculation otherwise
- FPU status word (FSTSW) used to store intermediate comparison results
- Comparison flags: bit 0x41 = (C0, C1, C3) from previous comparison operations

0x6FC2E821.name: ValidateFloatingPointRounding
0x6FC2E821.comment:
Validates whether a floating-point value satisfies integer rounding constraints.

Algorithm:
1. Load floating-point value from ST0 register (implicit x87 FPU parameter)
2. Round value to nearest integer using FRNDINT and compare with original
3. If value is not a perfect integer, return 0 (validation fails)
4. If value is integer, multiply by global scaling factor (0.5)
5. Round product to nearest integer and compare with original product
6. If product rounds exactly to integer, return 2 (complete success)
7. If product does not round exactly, return 1 (partial success)

Parameters:
ST0 (implicit float10): The floating-point value to validate

Returns:
EAX (int): 0=not integer, 1=integer but product not, 2=both integers

Special Cases:
Scaling factor 0.5 at g_dqFloatingPointScalingFactor

0x6FC2EA36.name: LoadAndValidateCachedFloatingPoint
0x6FC2EA36.comment:
Load and validate cached 10-byte floating-point value with lazy initialization.

Algorithm:
1. Clear floating-point stack by popping any existing values (FSTP ST0 x2)
2. Load 10-byte extended double from global cached value at 0x6fc41ea0
3. Check lazy initialization flag at stack frame offset -0x90
4. If flag is 0 (uninitialized), set flag to 1 to mark initialization done
5. Return the loaded floating-point value in ST0 register

Parameters:

Returns:
- long double: 10-byte extended double cached value in ST0 register

Special Cases:
- Initialization flag at EBP-0x90 prevents redundant initialization
- Global cache at 0x6fc41ea0 contains extended double value shared with pow()
- FPU stack cleared before load to prevent stack overflow exceptions

0x6FC2EA49.name: SetLocalStackFlag
0x6FC2EA49.comment:
Sets a flag byte in the caller's stack frame to indicate operation completion.

Algorithm:
1. Write byte value 1 to the caller's stack location at offset -0x90 from EBP
2. Return to caller

Parameters:
  Implicit: EBP register containing the base pointer of the calling function's stack frame

Returns:
  void: No return value. Function operates as a side effect, modifying a single byte at [EBP - 0x90].

Special Cases:
  - The target byte at [EBP - 0x90] must be pre-allocated in the caller's stack frame
  - The offset -0x90 (decimal -144) indicates the calling function has a large stack frame

  - Function is called via both CALL and JMP instructions, indicating use in tail-call optimization

0x6FC2EAC0.name: ComputePowerOfTwo
0x6FC2EAC0.comment:
Computes 2^exponent using x87 FPU extended-precision arithmetic.

Algorithm:
1. Load exponent value from FPU stack (ST0)
2. Round exponent to nearest integer (FRNDINT)
3. Calculate fractional part: exponent - round(exponent) (FSUBR)
4. Exchange stack: integer in ST0, fractional in ST1
5. Negate fractional part (FCHS)
6. Compute 2^(-fractional_part) - 1 using F2XM1 instruction
7. Load 1.0 and add to get 2^(-fractional_part) (FADDP)
8. Scale result by 2^integer_exponent using FSCALE
9. Store result to ST1 and pop FPU stack (FSTP)

Parameters:
exponent (float10): The exponent value for which to compute 2^exponent

Returns:
float10: 2^exponent as 10-byte extended-precision floating point value

Special Cases:
- Negative exponents: Correctly computes 2^(-x) as 1/2^x
- Zero exponent: Returns 1.0
- Large exponents: Extended precision allows computation of very large powers
- Fractional exponents: Precise computation via F2XM1 decomposition into integer and fractional parts

Notes:
This function uses the mathematical identity: 2^x = 2^(int_part + frac_part) = 2^int_part * 2^frac_part
The F2XM1 instruction efficiently computes 2^y - 1 for y in (-1, 1), enabling high precision.
FSCALE multiplies by 2^n by adjusting the exponent bits of the mantissa.

0x6FC2FDEC.name: ProcessFloatSpecialCases
0x6FC2FDEC.comment:
Processes floating-point values to handle special IEEE 754 cases (infinity, exceptions).

Algorithm:
1. Save EAX register to stack for later restoration
2. Load input float value from stack parameter
3. Extract exponent field by AND-ing with 0x7f800000 (IEEE 754 exponent mask)
4. Compare extracted exponent to 0x7f800000 (all exponent bits set = infinity)
5. If exponent equals 0x7f800000: jump to handle_infinity label for division
6. Read FPU status word using FNSTSW instruction to check processor state
7. Extract exception flags by AND-ing with 0x3800 (C2, C1, C0 bits in status word)
8. Check if any exception flags are set (JZ means no exceptions detected)
9. If no exceptions: jump to fpu_exception_path for normal processing
10. If exceptions detected: load float onto FPU stack and call error handler
11. For fpu_exception_path: exchange stack, allocate 12 bytes, store extended result
12. Load parameter with adjusted offset, call error handler, restore extended result
13. Deallocate temporary space and return with EAX restored
14. For handle_infinity: perform FPU division instruction and return

Parameters:
fValue (float): Input floating-point value in IEEE 754 32-bit format

Returns:
float in ST0/EAX: Result of special case processing

Special Cases:
- Infinity values (exponent = 0x7f800000): Handled via FPU divide instruction
- FPU exceptions: Routed through HandleFloatingPointErrorParameters callback
- Normal/denormalized: Processed through exception path with extended precision

0x6FC2FE38.name: HandleFloatingPointSpecialCase
0x6FC2FE38.comment:
Handles special IEEE 754 floating-point cases including NaN, infinity, and FPU exceptions.

Algorithm:
1. Extract exponent field (bits [30:20]) from doubleValue using mask 0x7ff00000
2. Compare exponent against NaN/Infinity marker (0x7ff00000)
3. If special value (NaN or Infinity), perform division and return result
4. Read FPU status word to check for exception flags
5. Mask and test exception flags (0x3800 covers Invalid Operation, Denormalized Operand, Zero Divide)
6. If exceptions detected, load operand, call error handler, and return result
7. If no exceptions, use alternate path: exchange registers, allocate temp stack, save extended double, load second operand, call error handler, restore and return
8. All return paths use __stdcall convention with callee stack cleanup (RET 0x8)

Parameters:
doubleValue - Input double-precision floating-point value to process (passed on stack)
exponentField - Pre-extracted exponent field bits [30:20] masked with 0x7ff00000 (passed on stack)

Returns:
double - Result of the operation, either division result for NaN/Infinity cases or output from error handler

Special Cases:
- IEEE 754 NaN/Infinity detection via exponent field = 0x7ff00000
- FPU exception handling for Invalid Operation (0x1000), Denormalized Operand (0x0800), Zero Divide (0x0400)
- Three distinct code paths: special value division, exception handling, and normal processing
- Uses extended-precision floating-point registers (ST0) for intermediate calculations
- Callers are responsible for loading exponent field; this function validates and processes accordingly

0x6FC2FEEC.name: ProcessFloatSpecialValue
0x6FC2FEEC.comment:
Processes special floating-point values (NaN, Infinity, denormalized numbers)

Algorithm:
1. Extract exponent bits from input using 0x7f800000 mask
2. Compare exponent against 0x7f800000 (special value indicator)
3. If all exponent bits set (0x7f800000), branch to special_value_handler
4. Check FPU status word flags (0x3800 mask) for exception state
5. If no exception flags set (JZ), execute normal_float_path with extended precision
6. If exception flags set, call CallFloatComputeHelper with standard precision
7. special_value_handler performs FDIVR operation on special values

Parameters:
inputValue (float): The floating-point value to process (passed on stack)

Returns:
float: The processed floating-point result in ST(0)

Special Cases:
- Special value indicator: 0x7f800000 (all exponent bits set - indicates NaN or Infinity)
- FPU status mask: 0x3800 (exception flags in bits 11-13)
- Uses extended double precision (80-bit) for intermediate calculations in normal path
- Special values trigger FDIVR operation for special handling
- Function cleanup removes 4 bytes from stack (RET 0x4)

0x6FC2FF38.name: HandleFloatOperation
0x6FC2FF38.comment:
Handles floating-point arithmetic operations with special value and exception handling.

Algorithm:
1. Load exponent bits from dwOperand2Bits parameter (upper 32 bits of second operand)
2. Mask to IEEE 754 exponent field (0x7ff00000) to check for special values
3. Compare against 0x7ff00000 to detect NaN or infinity (denormalized/special case)
4. If special value: return dOperand1 / ST0 (divide by FPU stack top value)
5. If not special: Read FPU status word via FNSTSW
6. Mask status word with 0x3800 to check exception flags (precision/underflow/overflow)
7. If exception flag set: Load dOperand1 from stack and call CallFloatComputeHelper
8. If no exception: Exchange FPU operands (FXCH), load second operand, call CallFloatComputeHelper
9. Return result as double from FPU ST0 register

Parameters:

  dwOperand2Bits (uint) - Second operand bits; exponent mask checked for special values

Returns:
  double - Result of floating-point operation from FPU ST0 register

Special Cases:
  - IEEE 754 special values (NaN, infinity) detected via exponent mask 0x7ff00000
  - FPU exceptions (precision/underflow/overflow) checked via status word mask 0x3800
  - Uses x87 FPU extended precision (float10) for intermediate calculations
  - Early return path for special values avoids standard processing
  - Two processing paths: exception handling vs normal operation with operand exchange

0x6FC30016.name: ComputeExtendedPrecisionRemainder
0x6FC30016.signature: float10 ComputeExtendedPrecisionRemainder(float10 * __return_storage_ptr__, float10 * pReturnStorage, uint mantissaLow, uint exponentAndMantissaHigh, ushort exponentAndSign)
0x6FC30016.comment:
Computes extended precision floating-point remainder using scaled iteration.

Algorithm:
1. Validate dividend and divisor exponents are in normal range (not denormalized or NaN)
2. Check that dividend mantissa is non-zero (all bits of mantissaLow and high mantissa)
3. If exponent difference > 0x3f: Use scaled iteration loop (5 iterations max)
   a. Load absolute values of dividend and divisor onto FPU stack
   b. Compare absolute values; if dividend <= divisor, subtract divisor from dividend
   c. Multiply dividend by 2^104 scaling factor from g_MantissaScaleFactor
   d. Decrement iteration counter; continue while scalingIterations != 0
4. If exponent difference <= 0x3f: Use single FPREM computation with adjusted exponent
   a. Load divisor with exponent reduced by (exponent_diff & 0x7) | 0x4
   b. Perform fmod: dividend - (dividend / divisor) * divisor
   c. Extract result mantissa components from FPU ST0
5. Apply sign bit to result (negate with FCHS if dividend was negative)
6. Handle FPU rounding mode flags and restore original control word
7. Return 80-bit remainder in ST0 register

Parameters:
pReturnStorage: Pointer to 80-bit float return storage location (output buffer)
mantissaLow: Low 32 bits of 80-bit dividend mantissa (bits 0-31 of mantissa)
exponentAndMantissaHigh: Bits 15-0 contain upper 16 bits of dividend mantissa; bits 31-16 contain dividend exponent
exponentAndSign: Bits 14-0 contain divisor exponent bits; bit 15 contains dividend sign (0=positive, 1=negative)

Stack parameters (via ESP offsets):
0x0C: Low 32 bits of divisor mantissa
0x10: High 32 bits of divisor mantissa (bits 15-0) and divisor exponent (bits 31-16)
0x14: Divisor exponent continuation bits (15-0) and sign bit (15)

Returns:

- Divisor exponent = 0 (denormalized): Handled by parent ComputeFloatingPointRemainder
- Exponent difference > 0x7ffe: Falls through to direct FPREM via direct_fprem_path
- Negative result: FCHS negation applied if dividend sign bit (bit 15) is set

0x6FC3021C.name: ComputeFloatingPointRemainder
0x6FC3021C.signature: float10 ComputeFloatingPointRemainder(float10 * __return_storage_ptr__, float10 dividend, float10 divisor)
0x6FC3021C.comment:
Computes the floating-point remainder (modulo) of two 80-bit extended precision numbers using the FPREM instruction with intelligent precision handling.

Algorithm:
1. Check divisor exponent field from high dword (bits 15-0 at offset +6)
2. If exponent field is zero (denormalized or special), call helper directly and return
3. Load operands from stack and extract dividend mantissa (low dword at offset +0, high dword at offset +4)
4. If both mantissa dwords are zero, use standard FPREM instruction and return
5. Preserve current FPU control word at stack offset +0x24
6. Extract divisor exponent bits using 0x7fff mask; compare against threshold 0x7fbe
7. If exponent <= 0x7fbe: scale both dividend and divisor by 2^104 constant at 0x6fc41f44 for precision preservation
8. If exponent > 0x7fbe: proceed without scaling (standard behavior for large exponents)
9. Restore modified FPU control word (rounding mode bits 0x33f or 0x300 set for FPU state control)
10. Call ComputeExtendedPrecisionRemainder helper with potentially scaled operands
11. Restore original FPU control word before returning

Parameters:
__return_storage_ptr__: float10 * - Pointer to return value storage (80-bit extended precision)
dividend: float10 - First operand (80-bit extended precision, passed in ST1)
divisor: float10 - Second operand (80-bit extended precision, passed in ST0)

Returns:
float10 * - Pointer to result storage; actual remainder value in ST0 FPU register

Special Cases:
- Divisor exponent field = 0 (denormalized/zero): delegates to helper immediately
- Dividend mantissa all zeros: uses standard FPREM fallback without helper
- Exponent difference > threshold (0x7fbe): standard precision (no scaling)
- Exponent difference <= threshold (0x7fbe): high precision (2^104 scaling for mantissa extraction)
- FPU rounding mode: modified during computation (0x33f bits for condition), restored after

0x6FC302CE.name: ComputeExtendedFloatingModulo
0x6FC302CE.signature: float10 ComputeExtendedFloatingModulo(float10 * __return_storage_ptr__, float10 ldDividend, float10 ldDivisor)
0x6FC302CE.comment:
Compute Extended-Precision Floating-Point Remainder

Algorithm:
1. Validate input parameters: Check for NaN/Inf conditions, verify neither operand has sign bit+exponent of 0x7FFF, ensure mantissa bits are properly formed
2. Extract exponent fields: Load exponent from high 15 bits of parameters, mask sign bits separately
3. Compute exponent difference: Calculate the difference between divisor and dividend exponents to determine scaling iterations
4. Choose scaling strategy: If exponent difference >= 64, use large-step iteration; otherwise use alternative threshold
5. For large exponent path (>= 64): Iteratively scale divisor by 2^(-20) until within range, then perform modulo
6. For small exponent path (< 64): Use direct FPREM1 with iterative scaling
7. Handle sign: Apply sign bit from original divisor to final remainder
8. Restore FPU state: Reset rounding mode and exception flags to saved state
9. Return remainder: Result in FPU ST(0) as 80-bit extended double

Parameters:
  dividend (ST[0] on entry): Extended precision dividend value
  divisor (ST[1] on entry): Extended precision divisor value

Returns:
  Extended double in FPU ST(0): Remainder value with sign applied

Special Cases:
  - NaN/Inf detection: Function validates bit patterns before proceeding, exits via validation_failed if invalid
  - Zero divisor: Early exit via validation checks at validation_failed label
  - Exponent normalization: Iterative scaling by 2^(-20) handles large exponent differences (>= 64)
  - Rounding mode: Temporarily sets rounding to nearest during FPREM execution
  - Exception flags: Preserves and restores FPU exception state
  - Sign handling: Applies divisor sign to remainder via FCHS instruction if sign bit set

Structure Layout:
  Extended Double Format (80-bit):
  Offset  Size  Field              Type     Description
  0       4     mantissaLow        uint32   Low 32 bits of 64-bit mantissa
  4       2     mantissaMid        uint16   Middle 16 bits of 64-bit mantissa
  6       2     exponentAndSign    uint16   15-bit exponent (bits 14-0) + 1-bit sign (bit 15)

Calling Convention: __cdecl (caller cleanup, return in FPU ST(0) for extended doubles)

0x6FC304D4.name: ComputeExtendedPrecisionModulo
0x6FC304D4.comment:
Extended-Precision Floating-Point Modulo Operation

Computes the modulo (remainder) of two extended-precision floating-point values using specialized FPU handling. This function accepts dividend and divisor in FPU registers ST0 and ST1 respectively, and returns the remainder in ST0. It implements special case handling for zero/denormalized divisors, exponent magnitude checking, and FPU control word manipulation to ensure correct rounding behavior.

Algorithm:
1. Save EDX register and allocate 48-byte workspace on stack
2. Store ST0 (dividend) at ESP+0x18 and ST1 (divisor) at ESP
3. Load divisor exponent from stack offset +6 and test against mask 0x7fff0000
4. If divisor exponent indicates invalid/zero value, call ComputeExtendedFloatingModulo error handler and return
5. Load both divisor values and test if both low/high dwords are zero
6. If both zero, jump to fprem_hardware_fallback for hardware FPREM execution
7. Exchange FPU registers and store divisor, set EDX flag 0x2 to indicate scaling
8. Save current FPU control word from offset ESP+0x24
9. Read control word, set mask bits 0x33f (round-toward-zero, mask all exceptions)
10. Store modified control word at ESP+0x28 and load into FPU
11. Load divisor exponent from offset ESP+0x20, mask to 15-bit (AND 0x7fff)
12. Compare exponent against threshold 0x7fbe
13. If exponent >= threshold, jump to exponent_overflow_branch for alternate processing
14. Set EDX flag 0x1 for normal scaling, multiply by g_dblFloatModuloScalingFactor
15. Store scaled values back to stack
16. Restore original FPU control word
17. Call ComputeExtendedFloatingModulo to complete remainder calculation
18. Restore EDX, deallocate stack, and return with result in ST0

Parameters:
  ST0 (implicit): Extended-precision dividend value (float10)
  ST1 (implicit): Extended-precision divisor value (float10)
  EDX (implicit): Working register, bits 0x1/0x2 track scaling state

Returns:
  ST0 (implicit): Extended-precision remainder (dividend mod divisor)

Special Cases:
  Zero/Invalid Divisor: Calls error handler ComputeExtendedFloatingModulo, returns through extraout_ST0
  Both Divisor Words Zero: Falls through to fprem_hardware_fallback, uses hardware FPREM instruction
  Denormalized Exponent: Scales by g_dblFloatModuloScalingFactor (0x6fc41f44)
  Exponent Overflow (>=0x7fbe): Uses alternate FPU control word masking (0x300 instead of 0x33f)

Global Data Referenced:
  g_dblFloatModuloScalingFactor @ 0x6fc41f44: Double precision scaling constant for denormalized exponents

Functions Called:
  ComputeExtendedFloatingModulo @ 0x6fc302ce: Completes remainder calculation after setup

0x6FC3095F.name: ParseDecimalString
0x6FC3095F.signature: void ParseDecimalString(char * pDecimalString, int stringLength, uint * pFixedPointResult)
0x6FC3095F.comment:
Converts decimal string to 96-bit fixed-point normalized representation

Algorithm:
1. Initialize 3-dword output array to zero
2. For each character in input string (stringLength iterations)
   - Shift 96-bit mantissa left by 4 bits (multiply by 16)
   - Load ASCII digit character and add to mantissa
3. Begin normalization: if high_dword is zero, shift right by 16-bit chunks
   - Each 16-bit right shift decrements exponent by 0x10
4. Continue normalization: shift left until high bit of high_dword is set
   - Each 1-bit left shift decrements exponent by 1
5. Store final exponent at offset +0xa in output array

Parameters:
pDecimalString (char*): Pointer to decimal digit string to parse
stringLength (int): Number of characters to process from string
pFixedPointResult (uint*): Pointer to 96-bit output array

Returns:
void - Result stored in pFixedPointResult array at offsets 0x0, 0x4, 0x8 (mantissa), 0xa (exponent)

Special Cases:
Empty string (stringLength=0) returns all zeros in output array
Initial exponent 0x404e is adjusted during normalization
Stack canary protection XORs guard seed with frame pointer
High bit test (0x8000) controls final normalization loop

0x6FC30A47.name: ConvertDecimalStringToLargeNumber
0x6FC30A47.signature: void ConvertDecimalStringToLargeNumber(uint * pResultNumber, int * pEndPos, byte * pInputString, int decimalExponent, int scaleFactor, int integralExponent, int allowExponent)
0x6FC30A47.comment:
Parses a decimal string into a normalized large number structure.

Algorithm:
1. Skip leading whitespace (space, tab, newline, carriage return)
2. Parse optional sign character ('+' or '-')
3. Transition to appropriate state based on character type (digit, decimal, null)
4. State 3 (Integral digits): collect significant digits into buffer, track overflow
5. State 4 (Decimal digits): skip leading zeros, collect fractional digits, adjust exponent
6. State 6 (Exponent marker): handle D/E/d/e character markers
7. State 7-9 (Exponent value): parse optional exponent sign and numeric value
8. Handle zero prefix normalization: skip leading/trailing zeros, adjust exponent downward
9. Trim overflow digits from buffer (max 24 digits), apply rounding if digit >= 5
10. Normalize digit buffer to large number via ParseDecimalString
11. Calculate final exponent: combine decimal position + parsed exponent ± integral/decimal adjustments
12. Check exponent bounds: must be between -5201 and 5201 (0xffffebb0 to 0x1450)
13. Scale mantissa via MultiplyLargeNumber: apply final exponent to mantissa
14. Store result structure: mantissa low word + mantissa high dword + exponent + sign flags

Parameters:
pResultNumber - Pointer to 12-byte result structure (mantissa: 6 bytes, exponent: 4 bytes, sign: 2 bytes)
pEndPos - Pointer to output: final position in input string after parsing
pInputString - Pointer to null-terminated input decimal string to parse
decimalExponent - Exponent adjustment for decimal point (scale factor)
scaleFactor - Additional exponent scaling for results without decimal point
integralExponent - Exponent adjustment when integral part is present
allowExponent - Flag: 0=disable E/D exponent markers, nonzero=enable

Returns:
void - Result written to pResultNumber structure via pointer:
  Offset 0x0: mantissa low word (undefined2)
  Offset 0x2: mantissa high dword (undefined4)
  Offset 0x6: exponent value (undefined4)
  Offset 0xA: sign and status flags (undefined2, upper bits contain sign)

Special Cases:
- Leading zeros: Stored as negative exponent adjustment, not in digit buffer
- Decimal without digits: Treated as 0.0
- Exponent overflow (>5201): Sets overflow status (0x7fff mantissa + 0x80000000 exponent)
- Exponent underflow (<-5201): Returns zero (0 mantissa + 0 exponent)
- Non-numeric input: Returns zero value
- Rounding: Applied when buffer contains >24 digits and overflow digit >= 5
- All zeros detected: Treated as zero value
- Stack canary verification: Compares XOR guard before/after to detect buffer overflows

Structure Layout (Output):
Offset  Size  Field Name              Type      Description
------  ----  ---------------------   --------  -----------------------
0x0     2     mantissaLow             uint16    Low word of 48-bit mantissa
0x2     4     mantissaHigh            uint32    High dword of 48-bit mantissa
0x6     4     exponentValue           int32     Adjusted exponent (-5201 to 5201)
0xA     2     signAndStatus           uint16    Sign bit in 0x8000, status in lower bits

0x6FC30E87.name: ConvertFloatingPointToDecimalString
0x6FC30E87.signature: void ConvertFloatingPointToDecimalString(uint mantissaLow, uint mantissaHigh, ushort exponent, int precision, byte flags, short * pOutputBuffer)
0x6FC30E87.comment:
Converts an IEEE 754 extended-precision floating-point number to decimal string representation.

Algorithm:
1. Initialize carry buffer (12 bytes) with sentinel values (0xcc, 0xfb, 0x3f)
2. Extract and set sign bit from exponent bit 15 to output[1] (0x20 positive, 0x2d negative)
3. Check for zero: if mantissa==0 AND exp==0, write "0" to output and return
4. Check for special exponent value 0x7fff:
   - If mantissa==0: write "INF" or "-INF" based on sign
   - If mantissa!=0 with bit 30 set: write "SNAN" for signaling NaN
   - If mantissa!=0 with bit 30 clear: write "QNAN" for quiet NaN
   - If specific pattern (exponent=0x7fff, mantissa=0xc0000000): write "IND" for indeterminate
5. For normal numbers, calculate internal exponent using formula: ((exp >> 8) + (mantissa_high >> 24)*2)*0x4d + offset*0x4d10
6. Normalize mantissa by scaling: left-shift by 8 positions, then right-shift if needed for denormalized
7. Generate decimal digits in precision+1 iterations: shift mantissa left 3 bits, add to carry, shift left again
8. Extract high byte of carry buffer as ASCII digit (carryBuf1f - 0xfb = decimal digit)
9. Apply rounding: if last digit >= '5' round up with carry propagation, else truncate trailing zeros
10. Write result structure: exponent(2 bytes) | sign(1 byte) | digitCount(1 byte) | digits | null terminator
11. Verify stack canary before return

Parameters:
  mantissaLow: Low 32 bits of 64-bit IEEE 754 mantissa
  mantissaHigh: High 32 bits of IEEE 754 mantissa with sign bit in bit 15 of exponent parameter
  exponent: 16-bit exponent field where bit 15 = sign, bits 0-14 = biased exponent (0x3fff bias)
  precision: Number of decimal digits to generate (clamped to 0-21 range)
  flags: Bit 0 set = add exponent to precision for adjusted conversion mode
  pOutputBuffer: Pointer to output structure containing exponent, sign, digit count, and digit string

Returns:
  None (results written directly to pOutputBuffer)

Special Cases:
  - Zero: mantissa==0 and exponent==0, returns "0" with exponent=0 and length=1
  - Positive infinity: exponent==0x7fff and mantissa==0 and sign=0, returns "INF"
  - Negative infinity: exponent==0x7fff and mantissa==0 and sign=1, returns "-INF"
  - Quiet NaN: exponent==0x7fff and mantissa!=0 with bit 30 clear, returns "QNAN"
  - Signaling NaN: exponent==0x7fff and mantissa!=0 with bit 30 set, returns "SNAN"
  - Indeterminate: exponent==0x7fff and mantissa==0xc0000000, returns "IND"
  - Denormalized: exponent==0 with mantissa!=0, treated as very small normal number
  - Rounding overflow: if rounding causes mantissa overflow, exponent incremented by 1

Structure Layout:
  Offset  Size  Field Name         Type      Description
  0       2     exponent           word      Biased exponent value
  2       1     signByte           byte      0x20 (positive) or 0x2d (negative)
  3       1     digitCount         byte      Number of decimal digits in string
  4       n     digits             char[n]   ASCII digit characters 0-9
  4+n     1     null               byte      Null terminator

0x6FC315EF.name: SetFloatingPointExceptionCode
0x6FC315EF.comment:
Sets the thread-local error number based on floating-point exception type.

Algorithm:
1. Load exception type parameter from stack (nExceptionType)
2. Check if exception type equals 1 (divide by zero):
   - If yes: Call GetThreadErrorNumberPointer() to get errno pointer
   - Set errno to 0x21 (EDOM - Domain Error)
   - Return
3. If exception type is not 1, check if it falls in range [2, 3]:
   - Check if nExceptionType > 1 (true for types 2, 3, 4, ...)
   - Check if nExceptionType < 4 (true for types 2, 3)
   - If both conditions true (type is 2 or 3):
     - Call GetThreadErrorNumberPointer() to get errno pointer
     - Set errno to 0x22 (ERANGE - Range Error)
     - Return
4. For all other exception types (0, 4+), return without setting errno

Parameters:
nExceptionType (int): Floating-point exception code
  - 1: Divide by zero (FP_DIVZERO) -> errno = 0x21 (EDOM)
  - 2: Invalid operation (FP_INVALID) -> errno = 0x22 (ERANGE)
  - 3: Overflow (FP_OVERFLOW) -> errno = 0x22 (ERANGE)
  - Other values: No action

Returns:
void (modifies errno via pointer returned by GetThreadErrorNumberPointer)

Special Cases:
- Exception code 1 and codes 2-3 both set errno, but to different values
- Exception codes outside ranges [1] and [2,3] do not modify errno
- Magic numbers: 0x21 = EDOM, 0x22 = ERANGE (POSIX error codes)
- All operations are based on the thread's error number location obtained from GetThreadErrorNumberPointer()

Dependencies:
GetThreadErrorNumberPointer(): Returns pointer to thread-local errno storage

0x6FC31652.name: InitializeFloatingPointExceptions
0x6FC31652.comment:
Initializes floating-point exception handling by loading special FPU values and exception handlers based on control flags.

Algorithm:
1. Save ECX register and allocate 8 bytes temporary storage on stack
2. Load fpExceptionFlags parameter from stack into CL register
3. If bit 0x01 set: Load extended double from g_extendedFpuValue1, convert to integer, store in stack
4. If bit 0x08 set: Load extended double from g_extendedFpuValue1, store as double on stack
5. If bit 0x10 set: Load extended double from g_extendedFpuValue2, store as double on stack
6. If bit 0x04 set: Generate infinity value (1.0/0.0) and pop from FPU stack
7. If bit 0x20 set: Load pi constant (FLDPI), store as double on stack
8. Pop temporary storage and return to caller

Parameters:
fpExceptionFlags (uchar): Control flags byte with bits indicating which FPU exception values to initialize:
  - Bit 0x01: Load and convert extended value from g_extendedFpuValue1 to integer
  - Bit 0x04: Generate infinity value (IEEE 754 division by zero)
  - Bit 0x08: Load extended value from g_extendedFpuValue1 as double
  - Bit 0x10: Load extended value from g_extendedFpuValue2 as double
  - Bit 0x20: Load pi constant (FLDPI)

Returns:
void - Does not return a value. Initializes FPU stack with exception handler values.

Special Cases:
Magic values:
  - g_extendedFpuValue1 (0x6fc42188): Extended double precision value (12 bytes)
  - g_extendedFpuValue2 (0x6fc42194): Extended double precision value (12 bytes)
  
FPU behavior:
  - Infinity calculation uses IEEE 754 division by zero which triggers FPU exception
  - WAIT instruction after each FSTP ensures FPU operation completes before next instruction
  - Stack allocation: Two PUSH ECX allocates 8 bytes for temporary FPU operand storage
  - FPU stack manipulation: Function leaves values on FPU stack for caller to use
  - Calling functions must manage FPU state and clean up stack after exception handling

Implementation notes:
  - Part of runtime floating-point exception initialization or signal handler setup
  - Used in exception handling path to initialize special IEEE 754 values (infinity, pi)
  - Multiple conditional branches allow selective initialization based on flags
  - Called from __handle_exc exception handler function

0x6FC316A8.name: MultiplyLargeNumbersWithValidation
0x6FC316A8.comment:
Multiplies two 96-bit large numbers with full validation and normalization.

Algorithm:
1. Load and validate input operands: extract exponents/signs from offset +10
2. XOR input signs to compute output sign bit (0x8000 mask)
3. Validate both exponents < 0x7fff and sum < 0xbffe (prevent overflow)
4. Check exponent sum >= 0x3fc0 (minimum magnitude threshold)
5. Handle zero operands: if either has zero mantissa, return zero result
6. Initialize 96-bit result accumulator (12 bytes at stack offset -0xc)
7. Execute nested multiplication loop: 5 outer iterations × 5 inner iterations
   a. For each outer iteration i (0-4): multiply result[i] by all multiplier words
   b. Inner loop: multiply pMultiplier[j] by pResult[i], add to accumulator[i+j]
   c. Propagate carries through accumulator words during multiplication
8. Add exponent bias (0xc002) and perform normalization
9. Normalize result by shifting mantissa left/right based on exponent
   a. If exponent < 1: right-shift mantissa, accumulate rounding bit
   b. If exponent > 0: left-shift mantissa until MSB set or exponent = 1
   c. Track rounding bit (set if any bits shifted out right)
10. Round result if rounding bit was set (set LSB of mantissa)
11. Validate result words don't overflow all-ones pattern (0xffffffff)
12. Write normalized result words back to pResult at offsets 0, 2, 6
13. Apply sign bit (0x8000) to exponent and store at offset +10
14. Check final exponent: if >= 0x7fff, set result to infinity

Parameters:
pResult: [EBP+0x8] = pointer to 96-bit large number (12 bytes)
  Offset 0-1: low word of mantissa
  Offset 2-5: middle 32 bits of mantissa
  Offset 6-9: high 32 bits with MSB at offset 10 bit 15
  Offset 10-11: exponent (15 bits) and sign bit (bit 15=0x8000)
pMultiplier: [EBP+0xc] = pointer to 96-bit large number (same format)

Returns: void; result written to pResult in-place with normalized mantissa and exponent

Special Cases:
- Zero result: if either operand has zero mantissa (all words = 0)
- Minimum magnitude: if exponent sum < 0x3fc0, result is zero
- Infinity: if exponent sum >= 0x7fff, result is infinity with sign bit preserved
- Rounding: mantissa rounded up if any bits shifted out during normalization
- Overflow detection: if rounded mantissa overflows, increment exponent and check again

Stack Usage: 0x30 bytes (48 decimal) for local variables and alignment

0x6FC318DE.name: MultiplyLargeNumber
0x6FC318DE.signature: void MultiplyLargeNumber(int * pResult, uint multiplier, int nBitWidth)
0x6FC318DE.comment:
Multiplies a large fixed-point number by an integer multiplier.

Algorithm:
1. Load and initialize security guard using XOR with frame pointer
2. Check if multiplier is zero - skip processing if true
3. Handle sign: negate multiplier if negative, select alternate table base
4. Check if nBitWidth is 0 - zero result if true
5. Loop through multiplier in 8-bit chunks:
   a. Shift multiplier right by 3 bits (divide by 8) to get next chunk
   b. Extract remainder (multiplier & 7) for table lookup
   c. Add 0x54 to table base for data section offset
   d. Calculate entry address from remainder * 0xc (12 bytes per entry)
   e. Check entry validity by testing bit 15 (0x8000) - skip if invalid
   f. Copy three DWORDs from table entry to temp buffer
   g. Call MultiplyLargeNumbers to multiply and accumulate result
6. Validate security guard XOR before return
7. Return to caller

Parameters:
- pResult: Pointer to result buffer (stores accumulated product)
- multiplier: Integer multiplier (positive or negative)
- nBitWidth: Bit width indicator; negative values select alternate table

Returns:
void - Result stored directly in pResult buffer

Special Cases:
- If nBitWidth == 0: pResult zeroed to 0
- If multiplier == 0: processing skipped entirely
- Negative multiplier uses g_MultiplyTableNegative (0x6fc422a0)
- Positive multiplier uses g_MultiplyTablePositive (0x6fc42140)
- Table entries marked with 0x8000 flag are skipped during processing
- Security guard uses XOR with frame pointer for stack corruption detection

Structure Layout:
Each table entry is 0xc (12) bytes containing three DWORDs:
  Offset 0x0: First coefficient (lower 2 bytes + upper 2 bytes split)
  Offset 0x4: Second coefficient (word at offset 0x4)
  Offset 0x8: Third coefficient (dword at offset 0x8)
Entries are accessed as: tableBase + 0x54 + (remainder * 0xc)

0x6FC31970.name: RemoveNodeFromList
0x6FC31970.comment:
Removes a node from a doubly-linked list.

This function serves as a wrapper/thunk for the UnlinkListNode function, providing

0x6FC328A0.name: DeleteGlobalCriticalSection
0x6FC328A0.comment:
Destroys the global critical section used for thread synchronization.

Algorithm:
1. Push the address of the global critical section (g_GlobalCriticalSection) onto the stack as parameter for DeleteCriticalSection API
2. Call Windows API DeleteCriticalSection to destroy the critical section object and release associated resources
3. Return to caller after cleanup complete

Returns:
void - No return value. This is a cleanup function that performs side effects only.

Parameters:
None - Uses the global g_GlobalCriticalSection directly.

Special Cases:
- The critical section at g_GlobalCriticalSection must be previously initialized with InitializeCriticalSection before this function is called
- Calling this function multiple times on the same critical section will cause undefined behavior
- This function is typically called during process shutdown or module cleanup
- The critical section should not be in use by any threads when this function is called

Structure Layout:
CRITICAL_SECTION at g_GlobalCriticalSection (24 bytes):
Offset  Size  Field Name       Type    Description
0x00    0x04  DebugInfo        void*   Pointer to debug info
0x04    0x04  LockCount        int     Lock recursion counter (-1 = unlocked)
0x08    0x04  RecursionCount   int     Number of times owned thread has acquired lock
0x0C    0x04  OwningThread     void*   Thread that owns the critical section
0x10    0x04  LockSemaphore    void*   Semaphore handle for thread synchronization
0x14    0x04  SpinCount        uint    Spin count for performance optimization
